articles.title: E-FILING EXTENSION - OFFICER INFORMATION diagnostic
articles.body_md:
# E-FILING EXTENSION - OFFICER INFORMATION diagnostic

```
E-FILING EXTENSION - OFFICER INFORMATION: You must enter all officer information in Organizer - General Information - Basic Return Information - Return Information - Officer Information. This includes officer name, title, date signed and phone number.
```

This happens when there's missing officer information or when the wrong signature date field was used.

## Solution

To resolve:

- Go to **Organizer**, **General Information**, and then **Basic Return Information**.
- Select **Return Information**.
- In the **OFFICER INFORMATION (MANDATORY)** section, make sure all entries are complete, such as officer name, title, date signed, and phone number. Make sure you use the correct date field (return vs extension).
- Perform a full recompute, and then recreate the e-file.

articles.title: F8868-908 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F8868-908 e-file error

## Error

```
If Form 8868, Item 'ExtensionReturnCd' is any value other than "03" (Form 4720 individual), "08" (Form 1041-A) or "10" (Form 5227), or Line 2, 'InitialReturnInd', 'FinalReturnInd', or 'AccountingPeriodChangeInd' checkbox is not checked, then tax year ending date ('TaxPeriodEndDt' specified in the Return Header) must match data in the e-file database. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule F8868-908).
```

## Cause

This error occurs because the tax year end date in the IRS database doesn't match the tax year end date in the e-file. For example, when the return has a calendar year end (12/31/YY) but the IRS database shows the client's year end as a fiscal year end (06/30/YY).

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer** then **General Information**.
- Select **Basic Return Information**.
- On the **Entity Information** tab, make sure the following fields are correct:


  - **Return Type**.
  - **EIN**.
  - **Fiscal Year Ending Date**.
- Select the **Return Information** tab.
- Make sure the **Return Type** checkboxes in the Check If section are marked.
- Go to **Organizer** then the **E-file** folder.
- Select **Extension**, **Additional Information**, then **Business Name Control**.
- If **Business name control (Override)** is completed, review Publication 4163 to check it's correct.
- If you corrected any fields, do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit the return.
- If you didn't make changes, contact the IRS e-help desk at 1-866-255-0654 to verify what they have on record.

articles.body_md:
# F990PF-905-01 e-file error

## Error

```
If Form 990-PF, Item G, "Initial return of a former public charity" checkbox is not checked, then the 'EIN' of the Filer in the Return Header must be established as a private foundation filer in the e-File database. (value 990PF, rule F990PF-905-01).
```

## Cause

The EIN and return type don't match what the IRS has in the e-File database.

## Solution if an initial return

- Go to **Organizer** then **General Information**.
- Select **Basic Return Information**.
- Select the **Return Information** tab.
- Mark the **Initial return** or **Initial Return of a former public charity** checkbox.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit the return.

## Solution if not an initial return

- Go to **Organizer** then **General Information**.
- Select **Basic Return Information**.
- Make sure the **EIN** is correct.


  - If you corrected the **EIN**, do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit the return.
  - If the **EIN** is correct, contact the IRS e-help desk at 1-866-255-0654. If you can't resolve it, you'll need to paper file.

# F990T-041 e-file error

```
* F990T-041: If Form 2220 is present in the return, then Form 990-T, 'ESPenaltyAmt' must be equal to Form 2220, 'TotalPenaltyAmt'.

- Select **Always sort Form 2220 with the tax return**.
- Perform a full recompute, re-create the e-file, and submit.

articles.title: R0000-058-01 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# R0000-058-01 e-file error

## Error

```
An XML document that represents a binary attachment must have a valid reference to an attached file. (value, rule R0000-58-01).
```

## Cause

The file name of the PDF attachment doesn't meet the IRS e-filing requirements.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, **E-File**, then **Return**.
- Select **Attachments**, **PDF Attachments**, then **Summary**.
- Select **Attach PDF**.
- Check that the file names of your PDF attachments meet the following e-file requirements:


  - 23 characters of less.
  - No spaces.
  - No special characters.
- If you need to change the file name of a PDF, delete it, change the file name, then reattach.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# R0000-901-01 e-file error

## Error

```
Filer's EIN and Name Control in the Return Header must match data in the e-File database. (value #########, rule R0000-901-01)
```

## Cause

The IRS e-File database has a different EIN and Name Control combination on file.

## Solution

- Check the name control:


  - Go to **Organizer**, **E-file**, then **Return**.
  - Select **Additional Information** then **Business Name Control**.
  - If **Business name control (Override)** is completed, review Publication 4163 to make sure it's correct.
- Check the **EIN**:


  - Select **General Information** then **Basic Return Information**.
  - Make sure the **EIN** is correct.
- If you corrected either field, recreate the e-file, and resubmit the return.
- If you're not overriding the name control and the EIN is correct, call the IRS e-help Desk at 866-255-0654 and verify the EIN.

- If you corrected either field, recreate the e-file, then resubmit the return.

articles.title: e-file an amended 1042 return
articles.body_md:
# e-file an amended 1042 return

You can amend and e-file a 1042 return.

- Make a copy of the original locator.
- In the new locator, go to **Organizer**, **Informational Forms**, **Withholding for Foreign Persons**, and then **Withholding for Foreign Persons**.
- Select **Amended**, and enter the necessary changes throughout the return.
- Next, go to **Organizer**, **Informational Forms**, **Withholding for Foreign Persons**, **Additional E-file Information**, and then **Additional Information**.
- Enter an explanation in the **Reasonable Cause for Superseded or Amended Return** field. This explanation is required for the IRS to accept the e-file.
- Perform a full re-compute, create the 1042 e-file, and then submit.

breadcrumb: e-file extension for Form 1042, Annual withholding tax return
articles.body_md:
# e-file extension for Form 1042, Annual withholding tax return

important

Beginning with tax year 2023, no duplicate locator's needed when needing to file an extension for both the regular return and the 1042 return.

- Go to **Organizer**, **Informational Forms**, **Withholding for Foreign Persons**, and then **Extension**.
- Select **File Form 7004**.
- Next go to **Federal 1042 E-file Extension**, and then **Enable Extension**.
- Select **Enable federal 1042 extension e-file**, enter the EFIN (electronic federal identification number), and then select the **Type of originator**.
- Next, go to **Signature Authorization**, and complete this information.
- If an extension payment's made through direct debit, go to **Additional Information** and **Bank Information** to complete any required information.
- To create the 1042 extension e-file, go to **Create E-file Extension**, and select **Create Federal 1042 Extension E-file**.
- Once a qualified extension e-file's created, submit the e-file using the **Federal 1042 Extension** jurisdiction description in the e-file submission.

articles.body_md:
# E-file Form 1042 withholding return

## Form 1042

Electronic filing of Form 1042's required for tax year 2023, for a withholding agent that's a financial institution. Otherwise, electronic filing of Form 1042's required for a withholding agent that's required to file 10 or more information returns, as described in [Regulations section 301.6011-2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/301.6011-2), during the year or that's a partnership with more than 100 partners.

## Waivers

Waivers may be granted in cases of undue hardship. A request for a waiver must be made in accordance with applicable IRS revenue procedures, publications, forms, instructions, or other guidance. The waiver request will specify the type of filing and the period to which it applies.

Find out more at [modernized e-file for Form 1042](https://www.irs.gov/e-file-providers/modernized-e-file-mef-for-form-1042) on the IRS website.

articles.title: F7004-003-03 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F7004-003-03 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 7004, the application for extension can only be filed after the Tax Period End Date ("TaxPeriodEndDate" specified in the "ReturnHeader") and on or before the due date of the return to which the extension applies as specified in the Form 7004 Date Charts in Publication 4164. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule F7004-003-03)
```

## Cause

The extension is e-filed either before the tax year end or after the return due date. For example, on a return with a tax year end of 3/31, you would receive this rejection if you filed an extension before 3/31 or after 6/15.

## Solution

Check for a mistake in the year-end date or an override in the extension date:

- Check the fiscal year end date:


  - Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
  - Select **Basic Return Information**.
  - On the **Entity Information** tab, check the **Fiscal year ending date**. If the date is wrong, fix it.
- Check the extension dates:


  - Go to the **Organizer**, then **Payments and Extensions**.
  - Select **Automatic Extensions**, then **7004 Basic Data**.
  - Make sure the override dates entered in the Dates section are correct. If any dates are wrong, fix them.
- Compare the extension file date, the fiscal year-end date, and the extension date.


  - If the extension is too early to file based on the client's tax year end, wait until the appropriate date to file the extension.
  - If the extension is late or if the return due date has passed, file the return instead of the extension.

articles.body_md:
# F7004-904-01 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 7004, the tax year ending date (TaxPeriodEndDt specified in the Return Header) must match the data in the e-file database unless one of the checkboxes in Line 5b - "Initial Return", "Final Return" or "Consolidated return to be filed" is checked. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule F7004-904-01)
```

## Cause

This error happens because the tax period end date, return type, or EIN in the IRS database doesn't match the information in the e-file.

## Solutions

- If the entity doesn't have a short tax year, check Form 7004, line 5b. Those checkboxes are for short year returns only.
- Check the tax period ending date, return type, and EIN. If they're correct, contact the IRS e-Help Desk at 866-255-0654.

# R0000-145-08 e-file error

## Error

```
For a return filed for tax year 2022, the tax period ending date in the Return Header must be [ one of following values ("20211231", "20220131", "20220228", "20220331", "20220430", "20220531", "20220630", "20220731", "20220831", "20220930", "20221031", "20221130") OR (1-3 days after the beginning of the month) OR (1-6 days before the end of the month) ] unless one of the following is true: 1. checkbox "Final Return" is checked. 2. checkbox "Initial Return" is checked. 3. return is a short year return, i.e., difference between the tax period beginning date and tax period ending date is less than 12 months.
```

## Cause

The tax period end date is invalid.

## Solution

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
- Select **Basic Return Information**.

articles.title: R0000-202 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# R0000-202 e-file error

## Error

```
If Form 965 is present in the return, then Form 965-A must be present. (rule R0000-202)
```

## Cause

Form 965-A is missing from the return.

## Solutions

If Forms 965 and 965-A are not needed, there is likely accidental data entry:

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **Income**.
- Open **§965 Inclusion of Deferred Foreign Inc**.
- Make sure the fields in this folder are correct. Remove any extra data entry.
- Do a Full Recompute, then recreate and re-transmit the return.

If the 965 and the 965-A are needed for the return:



- Go to the **Organizer**, then **Income**.
- Open **§965 Inclusion of Deferred Foreign Inc**.
- Go to **Payment Information** and open**2022 Inclusion Payment Information**.
- Check the fields in this screen. If none of the amounts are relevant, put "NONE" in those fields.
- Do a Full Recompute, then recreate and re-transmit the return.

# R0000-204 e-file error

```
R0000-204: If 'QualifiedBusinessIncomeDedAmt' in the return (1040, 1040NR, 1041) has a non-zero value, then one and only one Form 8995 or Form 8995A must be present in the return.

- Do a full recompute.
- Turn on the print selections.
- For Form 8995 Line 17, enter **NONE**.
- Do a full recompute.
- Recreate the e-file.

# R0000-900-01 e-file error

## Error

```
The return type indicated in the return header must match the return type established with the IRS for the EIN. (value, rule R0000-900-01)

The type of return on file with the IRS doesn't match the EIN included in the e-file.

- Select**Basic Return Information**, then **Entity Information**
- Check the fields and fix anything that's wrong. Then do a full recompute, re-create the electronic file, and resubmit.
- If the information is already correct, contact the IRS e-help Desk at 866-255-0654 for further assistance.

# R0000-901-01 e-file error

## Error

```
Filer's EIN and Name Control in the Return Header must match data in the e-File database. (value #########, rule R0000-901-01)
```

## Cause

The IRS e-File database has a different EIN and Name Control combination on file.

## Solution

- Check the name control.


  - Go to the **Organizer**, then **E-file**.
  - Select **Additional Information**, then **Business Name Control**.
  - If **Business name control (Override)** is completed, check Publication 4163 to make sure it's correct.
- Check the EIN/SSN


  - Go to **General Information**, then **Basic Return Information**.
  - Make sure that the **EIN** or **SSN** is correct.
- If you fix either field, re-create and retransmit the e-file.
- If you aren't overriding the name control and the EIN/SSN is correct, call the IRS e-help Desk at 866.255.0654 to find out what EIN/SSN they have on file.

articles.title: X0000-031 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# X0000-031 e-file error

## Error

```
Zip Entry names must conform to the guidelines in Publication 4164.
```

## Cause

A PDF attached to the return has an improper name or title.

## Solution

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **E-File**.
- Select **Attachments**, then **Summary**.
- Select **Attach PDF** and review your PDF attachments for the following e-file requirements:


  - Shorten the name of the attachments to 23 characters or less.
  - Remove any spaces in the file name.
  - Remove any special characters from the file name.
- Delete and reattach any PDF with an updated file name.
- Do a Full Recompute, recreate the e-file, and submit the return.

## Error

You cannot request a future payment date for returns submitted after the original due date. The Payment Date must be blank or the same as the return submitted date. articles.title: HIXML-001 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# HIXML-001 e-file error

```
The XML data has failed schema validation. The file name of supporting binary attachments must match their name in the XML file.
```

This happens when Hawaii’s PDF Attachment names don't match its e-file schema requirements.

## Solution

Hawaii has a set of specific names for PDFs that it allows as attachments to its e-filed returns. If those names are not used, and only when required, then the return will get rejected.

- In **Organizer**, select **States**.
- Select **Hawaii** and then **E-file**.
- In **Attachments**, go to **PDF Summary** to review the attached PDF names.

Hawaii e-file attachment file names need to match the names listed in the instructions, starting on page 9 of 11.

Remove incorrect PDF attachments, rename the files outside the program, and then reattach to the state. Full recompute and recreate the e-file.

|

|

|

|

**Special considerations** | None |

# 1040 Detroit electronic filing information

## City contact information

If you have specific questions about what you can e-file or about rejections you received, contact the city for more information.

**Michigan Department of Treasury**

Michigan Department of Treasury

Lansing, MI 48922

[www.michigan.gov/citytax](http://www.michigan.gov/citytax)

**Email**: [Treas\_CityTax@michigan.gov](mailto:Treas_CityTax@michigan.gov)

**Phone**: 517-636-5829

## City electronic filing details

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | None |


|

**E-filing mandate** | You must e-file if you are preparing more than 10 returns. |


|

**Accepts city-only filings** | Yes. Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default). Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics do not have to be cleared. |


|

**Return types accepted** | Resident  Part-year resident  Nonresident  Amended |


|

**Return types not accepted** | Extension  Estimate |


|

**Accepts returns with these conditions** | Refund  Zero balance  Balance due |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | No |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | Direct debit (EFW) |


|

**Signature requirements** | Detroit accepts federal PIN as the signature when you are e-filing with the federal return. If you are e-filing without a federal return, provide "shared secrets" to use PIN. |


|

**Driver's license requirements** | Optional |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current year and prior two years |


|

**Special considerations** | For tax year 2015 and later, Detroit returns are processed by the Michigan Department of Treasury. See Michigan Tax Preparer Handbook for Electronic Filing. |

Honolulu, HI 96809-0259

**Email**: [Tax.Efile@hawaii.gov](mailto:Tax.Efile@hawaii.gov)

**Phone**: 808-543-6814

**Tax Refund Inquiries**: Go to [tax.ehawaii.gov/hoihoi/refund.html](https://hitax.hawaii.gov/_/), or call 808-587-4242 or 800-222-3229

## State electronic filing details

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | Hawaii does not have a perfection period. Return needs to be resubmitted after correction. |


|

**E-filing mandate** |  |


|

**Accepts state-only filings** | Yes, Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default) - Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics do not have to be cleared |


|

**Return types accepted** | Resident  Part-year resident  Nonresident  Amended |


|

**Return types not accepted** | Estimate payments  Extension |


|

**Accepts returns with these conditions** | Refund  Zero balance  Balance due |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | Yes |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | Direct debit (EFW)  Check  ePayment  Note: Department of Taxation (DOTAX) requires that taxpayers with an annual tax liability of $100,000 or more and withholding taxpayers with tax liabilities of $40,000 or more to pay their taxes by Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT).  Please refer to Hawaii FAQs - "Mandatory Electronic Payment (EFT)" for more detail. <https://tax.hawaii.gov/geninfo/a2_b2_9tsm6/> |


|

**Signature requirements** | Hawaii considers the act of e-filing a signature. PIN is not allowed as signature. |


|

**Driver's license requirements** | Optional |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current tax year and two prior tax years |


|

**Special considerations** | Electronic filing information can be found at <https://tax.hawaii.gov/eservices/> |

## State electronic filing details

|

E-filing | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | 7 days |


|

**E-filing mandate** | Must e-file all individual income tax returns and extension requests when using software that supports e-file.  Opt-out / Waiver: None. If there is a reasonable cause, the preparer must maintain documentation. Important: client's desire to opt out of e-file is not a reasonable cause. View [cause.htm](https://www.tax.ny.gov/tp/efile/cause.htm). |


|

**Accepts state-only filings** | Yes. Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default). Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics do not have to be cleared. |


|

**Return types accepted** | Resident  Nonresident  Part-year  Amended  Extension  Estimate Payments (separate e-files)  IT-204-LL  NYC-202  NYC-1127 |


|

**Return types not accepted** | NYC-202 marked Amended Return |


|

**Accepts returns with these conditions** | Refund  Zero balance  Balance due |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | Yes |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | Direct debit (EFW)  Credit card  Check |


|

**Signature requirements** | Form TR-579-IT The taxpayer(s) and the ERO / Preparer must sign Form TR-579-IT, New York State E-file Authorization Signature for Forms IT-201, and IT203. Form TR-579-IT establishes that the taxpayer has reviewed his or her return, and authorizes the e-file of the return, and if an electronic funds withdrawal (for payment of the amount owed on the return) has been requested, it verifies that the taxpayer has authorized the electronic funds withdrawal. The ERO/Preparer must retain the TR-579-IT for three (3) years (do not mail it to the NYS Tax Department). The ERO/Preparer must also sign the return electronically by checking a New York State E-file Authorization box that indicates that they have read and agreed to our declaration certification language. Extension: Form IT-370 For a no Balance-Due Extension (Form IT-370) there is no signature requirement for the taxpayer or the ERO /Preparer. You are not required to complete or retain a TR-579.1-IT, New York State Taxpayer Authorization for Electronic Funds Withdrawal for Tax Year 2013 Form IT-370, for these transactions. For a Balance-Due Extension (Form IT-370) e-filed, you must also pay the balance due with an electronic funds withdrawal. The primary taxpayer must sign Form TR-579.1-IT, New York State Taxpayer Authorization for Electronic Funds Withdrawal for Tax Year [Tax Year] Form IT-370, to establish that he/she has authorized the ERO to nclude the information necessary for the Tax Department to initiate the withdrawal. The ERO is not required to sign the TR579-IT form or TR-579.1-IT form for these extensions; however, the ERO must retain the TR-579.1-IT for 3 years (do not mail it to the NYS Tax Department). The ERO/Preparer must also sign the extension electronically by checking the E-file Signature Authorization box that indicates that they have read and agreed to our declaration certification.  PIN allowed as signature: Yes |


|

**Drivers license requirements** | Required |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current tax year and two prior tax years |


|

**Special considerations** | See Publication 93, New York State Modernized e-File Guide for Return Preparers. To find the location of the document number on a New York-issued ID, refer to //dmv.ny.gov/id-card/sample-photo-documents |

E-filing information | Details |

|

|

No. Federal return must be filed electronically and accepted before WA e-file can be processed by WADOR.
Return types accepted
Working Families Tax Credit Application
Capital Gains Tax Return
Conditions for e-filing
Working Families Tax Credit amount must be greater than zero.
Capital Gains - Refund, Zero balance, Balance due
Direct deposit of refunds
Yes for Original application. No for Amended application.
Accepted forms of payment
Balance due is possible only for Amended application. WA DOR will send an invoice to the applicant.
Direct debit (EFW) is available for Capital Gains Tax Return.
Signature requirements
Uses the same PIN used for federal return.
Driver's license requirements
Optional
Supports PDF attachments
Yes
Tax years supported for e-filing
Working Family Tax Credit applications for tax years 2022 - 2024 will be accepted through December 31, 2025. Capital Gains tax returns for 2024 will be accepted through December 31, 2025.
Special considerations
See modernized e-file Handbook for Software Developers and Transmitters - Washington State.

articles.body_md:
# 1065 federal electronic filing information

## Contact information

If you have specific questions about what you can e-file or about rejections you received, contact the IRS for more information.

**Internal Revenue Service**

**Website**: <https://www.irs.gov/e-file-providers/e-file-for-tax-professionals>

**Phone**: 866-255-0654

## Electronic filing details

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | 10 calendar days for returns, 5 calendar days for extensions |


|

**E-filing mandate** | Partnerships with more than 100 partners and partnerships who file at least 10 returns annually must e-file. These returns include income tax, excise tax, employment tax, and information returns such as Forms W-2 and 1099.. |


|

**Return types accepted** | 1065, Partnership  8865, Foreign Partnership, when filed with the parent filer  Short year  Extension (for both 1065 and 8804)  Amended  Superseded |


|

**Return types not accepted** | 8865, Foreign Partnership, when filed separately  Returns with precomputed penalties and interest |


|

**Accepts returns with these conditions** | Refund/credit  No balance due  Balance due |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | No |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | Electronic funds withdrawal (EFW)  Electronic funds transfer (EFT)  Check by mail |


|

**Signature requirements** | Signed Form 8453-PE attached to the e-file as a PDF attachment before creating the e-file  ERO retains signed 8879-PE.  PIN and esignatures are allowed. |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current tax year and two prior tax years |


|

**Special considerations** | Refer to [IRS Publication 4163](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p4163.pdf) for detailed e-filing information for business returns. Refer to [Form and e-file approval status in UltraTax CS](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en-us/help/ultratax-cs/forms-approval-efile-status) for detailed information on which forms are and are not included in the return and extension electronic files. |

|

|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current tax year and two prior tax years |

# 1065 Michigan electronic filing information

## State contact information

If you have specific questions about what you can e-file or about rejections you received, contact the state for more information.

**Michigan Department of Treasury**

PO Box 30774

Lansing, MI 48929

**Website**: [www.michigan.gov/taxes/efile](https://www.michigan.gov/taxes/efile)

**Email**: [MIefile2D@michigan.gov](mailto:lgolliday@cityofbentonharbormi.gov)

**Phone**: 517-636-4450

**Tax Refund Inquiries**: 517-636-4657

## State electronic filing details

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | No |


|

**E-filing mandate** | Yes |


|

**Accepts state-only filings** | Yes - Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default) - Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics do not have to be cleared. |


|

**Return types accepted** | Partnership (MBT)  Amended (MBT) |


|

**Return types not accepted** | Composite  Extension  Consolidated  Composite Extension  Estimates  Extensions |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | No |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | ePayment |


|

**Signature requirements** | Form 4763 (MI-8879-MBT), Fed PIN, or Fed 8453 |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | No |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current tax year and two prior tax years |

# 1065 Mississippi electronic filing information

## State contact information

If you have specific questions about what you can e-file or about rejections you received, contact the state for more information.

**Mississippi Department of Revenue**

e-File Coordinator

PO Box 1033

Jackson, MS 39215

**Website**: [www.dor.ms.gov](https://www.dor.ms.gov/)

**Email**: [efile@dor.ms.gov](mailto:efile@dor.ms.gov)

**Phone**: 601-923-7700

## State electronic filing details

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | 10 days |


|

**E-filing mandate** | Yes |


|

**Accepts state-only filings** | Yes - Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default) - Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics do not have to be cleared. |


|

**Return types accepted** | Partnership  Amended  Extensions |


|

**Return types not accepted** | Estimate Payments  Consolidated  Composite  Composite Extension |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | No |

|

|

|

E-filing information | Details |


| --- | --- |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|

**Grace period** | 24 hours |


|

**E-filing mandate** | Form 1120ME if a corporation has more than $5,000,000 in assets at the end of the year.  For returns filed in calendar year 2025 and subsequent years, corporations and a preparer for such corporation required to file the federal corporate return electronically for the taxable year must also file the Maine Form 1120ME electronically.  Form 941P-ME for all corporations. |


|

**Accepts state-only filings** | Yes. Attach the federal XML created for this State (Default). Only Federal e-file validation errors have to be cleared. E-file Reject Diagnostics don’t have to be cleared |

|

**Return types not accepted** | Short year Form 941P-ME  Extension  Composite |


|

**Accepts returns with these conditions** | Refund  Zero balance  Balance due |


|

**Direct deposit of refunds** | Yes, only to checking accounts for Form 1120-ME, and limited to $20,000. |


|

**Accepted forms of payment** | Direct debit (EFW)  Electronic funds transfer (EFT)  Check by mail |


|

**Signature requirements** | Maine doesn't require a signature document. However, the taxpayer needs to verify the information in the return, and the ERO needs to provide a perjury statement or attestation to the taxpayer prior to the time of submission. |


|

**Supports PDF attachments** | Yes |


|

**Tax year(s) supported for e-filing** | Current and 2 prior tax years for corporate and withholding return |


|

**Special considerations** | N/A |

articles.title: E-file application summary and requirements
articles.body_md:
# E-file application summary and requirements

Submit your IRS e-file application summary to verify your eligibility for electronic tax filing.

The IRS, state tax agencies, and private companies created the Security Summit partnership to protect taxpayers and tax preparers. This partnership makes it easier to verify tax return preparers and transmitters who use Electronic Filing Identification Numbers (EFINs).

Your provider will need to keep a copy of your e-file application summary.

note

If you're a new customer or you received a new EFIN from the IRS, submit your e-file application summary to Thomson Reuters to file returns electronically.

## Obtain your e-file application summary

You'll need to provide a copy of your IRS e-file application summary before you can e-file tax returns. Sign in to your e-services account to get it. This summary shows the application you submitted and the IRS approved for your EFIN number. It lets Thomson Reuters verify that you're eligible to file returns electronically.

Once Thomson Reuters verifies your EFIN, you can file returns electronically. If your firm uses the IRS e-Services program, you can use Thomson Reuters to e-file.

note

Only the person who received the EFIN from the IRS can access the e-file summary. For help with your IRS e-services portal or sign-in issues, call the IRS e-Help Desk at 866-255-0654.

## Submit your e-file application summary

In GoSystem Tax, select **Admin**, then **EFIN Validation**.

In ONESOURCE Income Tax, go to 

**Tools****Admin Tools****EFIN Validation**

.

On the 

EFIN Validation

 screen, complete all required fields and upload your EFIN Application Summary. This document must match the information on file with the IRS for successful e-filing.

breadcrumb: Opt out of e-filing a return with Form 8948
articles.body_md:
# Opt out of e-filing a return with Form 8948

Use Form 8948 to explain why you're filing a return on paper instead of electronically.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Additional Information****E-file Opt Out**

  .
- Select **Preparer Explanation**, then select the reason for not e-filing the return:

  * **The taxpayer has selected to file on paper and the return is prepared by the preparer, but will be submitted by mail by the taxpayer.** A taxpayer statement prints when you select this option.
  * **The preparer's a member of a recognized religious group that is opposed to its members using e-file**.
  * **The preparer applied for and received an approved undue hardship waiver.** Enter the waiver reference number and approval letter date.
  * **The return was rejected and the reject condition couldn't be resolved.** Enter the reject code and the number of attempts to solve the rejection.
  * **The tax product doesn't support the e-filing of one or more forms or schedules**.
- If none of these reasons apply, select **Other** and describe the circumstances.

articles.body_md:
# Set up 1040 e-file signature authorization

Let taxpayers sign tax returns electronically by selecting a signature authorization method and entering PIN information in the Organizer.

Signature authorization lets taxpayers sign their tax returns electronically for e-filing. Enter signature authorization information in the Organizer before creating and submitting the electronic file.

2 signature authorization methods are available:

* **Practitioner PIN (Form 8879)** - The Electronic Return Originator (ERO) generates a 5-digit PIN for the taxpayer and spouse. This method requires Form 8879.
* **Self-select PIN** - The taxpayer select their own 5-digit PIN using their prior year AGI or self-select PIN for verification.

After selecting a signature authorization method, enter the PIN information in the Organizer.

articles.title: Choose a PIN method for 1040 e-file signature authorization
breadcrumb: Choose a PIN method for 1040 e-file signature authorization
articles.body_md:
# Choose a PIN method for 1040 e-file signature authorization

Select a PIN method based on taxpayer eligibility and filing requirements.

The PIN is any 5 numbers (except all zeros) that the taxpayer selects as their electronic signature. You can select PIN options in 

**Organizer****E-file****Signature Authorization**

.

## Self-select PIN method

The self-select PIN method lets taxpayers enter their own PIN as their electronic signature.

important

Not all taxpayers are eligible for the self-select PIN method. First-time filers under age 16 and taxpayers who filed Forms 1040-NR or 1040-SS in the prior year can't use this method.

These taxpayers are eligible to use the self-select PIN method:

* Taxpayers who filed Form 1040, 1040PR, or telefile in the prior tax year
* Taxpayers who didn’t have a filing requirement for the prior tax year but have filed previously
* First-time filers who are 16 or older on or before December 31
* Military personnel residing overseas with APO/FPO addresses
* Taxpayers residing in American possessions (Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, Northern Marianas) or with foreign country addresses

These taxpayers are not eligible to use the self-select PIN method:

* First-time filers under age 16
* Taxpayers who filed Forms 1040-NR or 1040-SS for the prior tax year

## Practitioner PIN method

If you use the practitioner PIN method, you can enter or generate the taxpayer's PIN for them. This method doesn't require a prior year AGI, a self-selected PIN, or birth dates for verification.

EROs (electronic return originators) need to complete [Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8879), including Part III, and retain it for 3 years.

note

If your client can't return to your office to enter their self-selected PIN, they can return the signed Form 8879 personally, by mail, or by fax.

# Use a self-selected PIN for e-file authorization

Set up self-select PIN authorization by entering taxpayer PINs and prior year information for identity verification.

Go to 

**Organizer****E-file****Signature Authorization**

 and select **Self-select PIN** as the PIN type.

- Select who entered the PIN: **ERO (Electronic Return Originator)** or **taxpayer/spouse**.

note

Form 8879 won’t print when using the self-selected PIN method. The taxpayer uses their self-selected PIN and prior year information to sign electronically.

articles.title: Choose signature options for e-filed 1041 returns
breadcrumb: Choose signature options for e-filed 1041 returns
articles.body_md:
# Choose signature options for e-filed 1041 returns

Select and configure signature authorization methods for filing Form 1041 returns electronically using either the Practitioner PIN method or Form 8453-FE.

You can sign a return before e-filing it using 1 of 2 methods:

- **Practitioner PIN method**: Taxpayers who use an ERO (electronic return originator) sign their returns using a 5-digit PIN. Both the taxpayer and practitioner must sign Form 8879-F, IRS e-file Signature Authorization.
- **Form 8453-FE**: The system sends Form 8453-FE electronically with the return to the IRS instead of requiring a paper signature.

Follow these steps to configure signature options:

- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Signature Authorization**

  .
- On the **Signature Authorization** screen, select who entered the **PIN** and choose the **Signature Option**.

  * If you select **Fiduciary or Officer** and **Form 8453-FE**, Form 8879 won’t print.
  * If you select **Preparer or ERO**, Form 8879-F prints for the fiduciary to sign. Keep the signed Form 8879-F for 3 years. Don't send it to the IRS.
- In the **PIN Information** section, select how to create and enter the PIN:

  * **Randomly generate fiduciary or officer PIN**: Use this option if you use the Practitioner PIN method.
  * **Use first 5 numbers of firm EIN as ERO PIN**: After you recompute the return, the PINs will appear.
  * **Print fiduciary PIN on the Form 1041, Page 1 signature line**: Select this option to display the PIN on the printed form.
- To enter PINs manually, use the **Fiduciary PIN**, **ERO PIN**, and **Date PINs entered** fields.

  note

  Enter the 5-digit PIN (the number can't be all zeros) for the fiduciary (if filing jointly).

articles.title: Signature requirements for 1065 partnership e-filed returns
breadcrumb: Signature requirements for 1065 partnership e-filed returns
articles.body_md:
# Signature requirements for 1065 partnership e-filed returns

Understand the signature requirements for partners, EROs, and paid preparers when e-filing partnership returns using Form 8453-PE or Form 8879-PE.

## Partner signature

The partnership must designate a principal of the firm responsible to sign the partnership return. The designated partner must sign and date the Declaration of Taxpayer on either Form 84583-PE or Form 8879-PE before e-filing to authorize IRS submission.

In the declaration, the taxpayer states under penalties of perjury that the return is true, correct, and complete. The taxpayer also consents to let the IRS share return information and e-file results with the taxpayer's Authorized IRS e-file Providers, including Transmitters and Electronic Return Originators (EROs).

## ERO signature

The ERO must thoroughly read the declaration, then sign and complete the requested information in the Declaration of Electronic Return Originator (ERO) and the Paid Preparer section.

## Paid preparer signature

If someone prepares the return for a fee, the paid preparer must also sign the jurat form (Form 8453-PE).

articles.title: Electronic signature requirements for EFAST2 filings
breadcrumb: Electronic signature requirements for EFAST2 filings
articles.body_md:
# Electronic signature requirements for EFAST2 filings

Understand the electronic signature requirements for EFAST2 filings, including signer credentials and signature combinations for different forms.

Review the EFAST2 electronic signature requirements before you file.

## EFAST2 signature credentials

EFAST2 assigns each signer two identifiers: a PIN and a User ID. Together, the PIN and User ID act as the user's electronic signature.

## Required signatures

A filing may require as few as one or as many as 4 signatures from the following parties: Plan Administrator, Employer/Plan Sponsor, authorized service provider for eSignature, and/or Direct Filing Entities (DFE).

Form 5500-SF filings need to have a signature from either the Plan Administrator and/or the Employer/Plan Sponsor or authorized service provider.

note

If you serve as both the Plan Sponsor and the Plan Administrator, you only need to sign as the Plan Administrator on the Plan Administrator line.

# Sign a Form 990 e-file

Sign exempt organization federal tax returns electronically using a practitioner PIN or Form 8453-EO.

Tax practitioners can sign exempt organization federal tax returns electronically using a personal identification number (PIN). You may use either the practitioner PIN method or Form 8453-EO.

Follow these steps to sign a 990 e-file:

- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Return****Signature Authorization**

  .
- Select **PIN options**.
- On the 

  Signature Authorization

   screen, select one of these options:

  * **Form 8879-TE - Practitioner PIN**: The taxpayer and ERO will each select a PIN (or use the auto-generate option) to sign the return. As the ERO, you'll complete Form 8879-EO and retain it for 3 years.
  * **Form 8453-TE - scanned signature document**: The ERO completes and prints Form 8453-EO. Have all required parties sign the form, scan it into a PDF document, and attach it as a binary attachment. Limit the PDF file name to 23 characters.
- If you chose to use the practitioner PIN method, indicate who entered the PIN: ERO or Officer. You can also select to generate the PINs automatically.
- Enter the PINs.

articles.title: State e-file workflow
articles.body_md:
# State e-file workflow

Track your state return through each step of the electronic filing process, from transmission to final acknowledgment.

Understanding the state e-file workflow helps you track where your return is in the submission process. All state returns follow this path:

- Thomson Reuters transmits your return (including any state returns) to the IRS.
- The IRS e-file system runs validation checks. If the return passes validation, the IRS sends it to the state. If the return fails validation, the IRS rejects it.
- The state retrieves your return from the IRS e-file system and sends a receipt confirmation.
- The state processes your return and sends an acknowledgment (accepted or rejected) back to the IRS e-file system.
- The system retrieves the acknowledgment and makes it available to you in the **E-file Status Report**.

note

You can track your return's progress at any time by checking the **E-file Status Report**.

  3. The state retrieves your return from the IRS e-file system and sends a receipt confirmation.

  5. The system retrieves the acknowledgment and makes it available to you in the
    E-file Status Report
    .
note
You can track your return's progress at any time by checking the
E-file Status Report
.

articles.title: Submit linked and unlinked state returns
breadcrumb: Submit linked and unlinked state returns
articles.body_md:
# Submit linked and unlinked state returns

Submit state returns as linked or unlinked filings, and resolve common reject codes for state e-file submissions.

## Linked filing

Linked filing connects your state tax return to your federal tax return and submits them either simultaneously or soon after.

- Go to the 

  Create Electronic Filing Batch

   screen, then go to the **Select Return/Extension** section.
- Select **Check Federal Return** and **Check State Return** for the federal and state returns.

  ![](/content/dam/helpandsupp/en-us/Topics/ONESOURCE-family/images/linked-filing.png/_jcr_content/renditions/original)
- Select the **Qualified** returns to submit.

You can submit linked returns using 2 methods, depending on whether the IRS has already accepted your federal return.

****For federal returns that the IRS has already accepted**:**

- Create the qualified state e-file.
- Follow each step of the 

  Steps of Electronic Filing

   screens in the State Organizer.
- Ensure your federal return details are accurate. You need this to link your state and federal returns and to attach a federal return copy.
- Close the return after creating the qualified state return.
- On the 

  Create Electronic Filing Batch

   screen, in the **Select Return/Extension** section, select both the **federal ready to send** and the **states ready to send** options.

**For Federal returns that **the IRS hasn't yet accepted**:**

- Create the qualified state e-file.
- Follow each step of the 

  Steps of Electronic Filing

   screens in the State Organizer.
- Ensure your federal return details are accurate. You need this to link your state and federal returns and to attach a federal return copy.
- Close the return after creating the qualified state return.
- On the 

  Create Electronic Filing Batch

   screen, in the **Select Return/Extension** section, select both the **federal ready to send** and the **states ready to send** options.

Thomson Reuters first submits your federal return while holding your state return. When the IRS accepts your federal return, Thomson Reuters submits your state return as a linked filing. If the IRS rejects your federal return, your state return is also rejected. If this happens, correct your federal return and resubmit both returns.

## Unlinked filing

Unlinked filing lets you submit your state return independently, without directly connecting it to a federal return submission.

- Go to the 

  Create Electronic Filing Batch

   screen, then go to the **Select Return/Extension** section.
- Select **Check State Return**.
- Select the **Qualified** returns to submit.

  ![](/content/dam/helpandsupp/en-us/Topics/ONESOURCE-family/images/unlinked-filing.png/_jcr_content/renditions/original)

**To submit an unlinked filing:**

- On the 

  Copy of Federal Return

   screen within the State Organizer or Common State Organizer, select **State Only Copy of the Federal Return**.
- Create the qualified state e-file by following each step on the State Organizer's 

  Steps of Electronic Filing

   screens.
- Ensure your federal return details are accurate. You need this to link your state and federal returns and to attach a federal return copy.
- Close the return after creating the qualified state return.
- On the 

  Create Electronic Filing Batch

   screen, in the **Select Return/Extension** section, select **states ready to send**.

## Reject codes

Thomson Reuters may reject otherwise qualified state returns if conditions exist that would cause MeF to reject the return. These reject codes are specific to MeF filing:

* **Error 9501**: For both linked and unlinked submissions. The system was checking in the state return, but couldn’t find a federal file.
* **Error 9502**: For linked submissions only. The IRS rejected the federal return and the state return was dependent on the IRS accepting the federal return.
* **Error 9974**: Only unlinked submissions can be made. This error occurs if you selected **Create a federal copy for state only return**. To correct this error:


  * Go to 

    **Organizer****States****Common State****Fed-state Electronic Filing Options**

    .
  * Select **Federal Copy State Only Opt (Optional)- Federal Copy for state Only Return**.
  * Send returns to e-file when they're ready to submit.
  * Go to the 

    Send Return

     screen. Mark only **State Ready to send**.
  * Submit the selected returns as **State Only**.

    note

    If you don’t submit this as a **State Only** return, the system will reject the return.

articles.title: Submit linked or unlinked state returns
breadcrumb: Submit linked or unlinked state returns
articles.body_md:
# Submit linked or unlinked state returns

Submit state returns as linked or unlinked to federal returns, with different validation and transmission processes for each type.

State e-file accepts 2 types of state submissions:

* Linked
* Unlinked

Regardless of which type you select, the system transmits all state returns to the federal e-file system before it forwards them to the state taxing authority.

You decide to link or unlink the federal and state returns when you create the e-file batch and send it to Thomson Reuters.

## Linked submission

A linked state return connects to a federal return and includes the federal return's submission ID. This is also called a federal/state submission. When you transmit linked returns, the system transmits the federal return first and holds the state return until the IRS accepts or rejects the federal return.

* If the IRS rejects the federal return, the system also rejects the state return. The transmitter receives acknowledgments about the rejection, but the system doesn't notify the state.
* If the IRS accepts the federal return, the system transmits the state return. The e-file program performs validation checks before sending to the state taxing authority.
* The state can still reject the state return if it fails the IRS validation checks or if the state taxing authority rejects it.

## Unlinked submission

When you don't link federal and state returns, the system submits the state return independently. It doesn't include the federal return's submission ID. The system doesn't hold it until the IRS accepts the federal return. The IRS e-file system performs minimal validation checks on the state submission before forwarding it to the state taxing authority.

The state can still reject the state return if it fails the minimal validation checks or if the state taxing authority rejects the return.

The state may accept the state return before the IRS accepts the federal return.

important

Be careful if you materially change the federal return to get IRS acceptance. The federal return you filed with the IRS would no longer match the federal return you filed with the state. If this happens, you may need to file an amended state return.

This type of submission is also referred to as a state standalone submission.

articles.title: E-file Alabama and New York consolidated returns
breadcrumb: E-file Alabama and New York consolidated returns
articles.body_md:
# E-file Alabama and New York consolidated returns

Submit consolidated 1065 and 1120 returns for Alabama and New York by e-filing the top-level return together with all member returns.

Alabama and New York require you to e-file 1065 and 1120 business returns separately for each member of a consolidated group. So when a lower-member return in either state is part of a consolidated return, you'll need to qualify and submit both the top-level and each lower-member return separately.

We've included a search feature unique to these 2 states to help you complete this process. To e-file either Alabama or New York, select **Returns Processing**, **E-file**, then **Select Returns**.

## Consol display option

- For **Select Returns/Extension** options, select **Consol Display** for the **Display Type**.
- Mark the **States/Cities ready to send** checkbox, then select the state and return e-file type from the dropdown.
- Review the results, which show the top returns and member returns for the type you selected.
- Select the link for the top return to submit it along with the lower members.
- Mark the **Select** checkbox for the return, then select **Submit for E-file** to complete the e-file submission process.
- The system submits the top return and all members of the selected return to the taxing authority.

## Regular display option

- For **Select Returns/Extension** options, select **Regular Display** for the **Display Type**.
- Mark the **States/Cities ready to send** checkbox, then select the state and return e-file type from the dropdown.

  note

  The system grays out all checkboxes for consolidated returns and makes them unavailable to submit for e-file. A message displays prompting you to submit this return with the entire consolidated group.
- Select the link on the subsidiary return ID.
- Mark the checkbox for the return to submit for e-file.

## Single Alabama or New York forms

If you select the **Regular Display** option, you can submit single returns from the 

Initial Returns

 screen. Select the link or mark the checkbox in the **Selected** column.

## Regular display with all states option

When you select **All States/Cities E-file**, the results on the 

Returns

 screen display all qualified states and cities for all entity types.

You can submit single company returns with single Alabama or New York the same way as other single company jurisdictions. Mark the **All** checkbox or the **Select** checkbox, or select the link for the single company states.

## Considerations for other states

For consolidation companies with states other than Alabama or New York, you can submit an e-file from 2 locations:

- The 

  Returns

   screen
- The **Alabama** or **New York** links

**Returns screen**

On this screen, the system shows all qualified states and makes them available for you to submit for e-file except for Alabama and New York.

* Mark the **Select** option next to the states.
* Select **Submit For E-File**.
* You can submit all states other than the 2 mandatory states to their respective jurisdictions from the 

  Initial Returns

   screen.

## Alabama or New York links

If the system grays out an Alabama or New York consolidated return on the 

Initial Returns

 screen, you need to select the **Alabama** or **New York** link. You'll get a list of qualified states, and you can submit the Alabama or New York parent, subsidiary, and consolidated returns as well.

- On the 

  Initial Returns

   screen, review and mark the **Select** checkbox next to the following:


  * Each jurisdiction that's part of your Alabama or New York consolidated group.
  * All Alabama or New York consolidated group members.
- Select **Submit For E-file** to submit all the state returns you selected on this screen.
- Alternatively, you can select the jurisdiction's link to submit the returns if you prefer.

important

Access consolidated New York and Alabama from the Alabama or New York links to e-file the parent, subsidiary, and consolidated returns. If you select **Select All** on the initial 

Returns

 screen, the system won't submit the Alabama and New York consolidations.

articles.title: Create a federal e-file
articles.body_md:
# Create a federal e-file

Create a federal e-file XML file in the Organizer and review the file status and formatting requirements.

Follow these steps to create a federal e-file:

- In **Organizer**, select **Federal E-file**.
- Select **Create E-file**.

  The system creates an XML file that includes a date and time stamp, along with the e-file status.

* You'll need to clear any XML file errors before submitting the e-file.
* You can only create 1 XML file at a time in the Organizer.
* The system presents consolidated returns only in stacked format.
* The IRS requires that cross-tie print options don't apply to electronic filing.
* Supporting statements might not appear in the same order as they would print for a return.
* Non-numerical information may appear at the entity level where you entered it.
* The system doesn't include the PDF attachment in the PDF reader, but the return displays the attachment information in the **Binary Attachment** section.

articles.title: E-file returns and extensions in the Organizer
breadcrumb: E-file returns and extensions in the Organizer
articles.body_md:
# E-file returns and extensions in the Organizer

Follow these steps to turn on e-file, select a signature method, attach documents, validate the return, and transmit it to the IRS using Organizer.

Complete the following steps to e-file a return and extension in the Organizer.

- In the Organizer, select **Federal e-file**, then **Enable** to turn on e-file.
- Select a signature authorization method: **Form 8879 Practitioner PIN** or **Form 8453 scanned signature document**.
- Attach supporting documents in PDF format, such as Form 8453, then enter general dependencies for the return.
- Attach separate XML files for international forms:

  * Form 5471
  * Binary attachments for Forms 5471 and 8865
- Review additional information specific to the e-file return, such as business name control and foreign entity identification.
- Generate a validation file to check for errors and validate the XML file against the IRS schemas.
- Select **Create E-File** to create the e-file.
- Review the status of the XML file, including the date and time stamp, validation errors, and file name.
- Review e-file diagnostics.
- Perform a full recompute.
- Review the return.
- Use the browser to transmit the e-file to the IRS.
- Check the e-file status to verify that the IRS has accepted or rejected the return.

note

**Additional requirements**



* If the return includes international forms, aggregate them into the primary return XML file.
* If the return is a mixed return (for example, it includes a life insurance company or property and casualty Insurance company), create a mixed return XML file.
* If you're filing a short period return, attach a Form 1128 to the return.
* If you selected the **Practitioner PIN method**, include a Form 8879 with the e-file.

**IRS e-filing requirements**

The IRS requires that your return meets the following criteria:

* **Business rules**: The return must include all required forms and schedules.
* **Schemas**: The return needs to comply with IRS schemas, which define the format and structure of the XML file.
* **Validation**: The return needs to pass validation checks to ensure it meets IRS requirements.

articles.title: Compare FBAR and MeF e-file systems
breadcrumb: Compare FBAR and MeF e-file systems
articles.body_md:
# Compare FBAR and MeF e-file systems

Review the key differences between FBAR and MeF e-file systems for transmission, format, attachments, EFIN requirements, signatures, and error handling.

The following table shows the key differences between FBAR and MeF e-file systems regarding transmission, format, attachments, EFIN, signature, and errors.

|

articles.title: Create an FBAR e-file
articles.body_md:
# Create an FBAR e-file

Complete, validate, and create FBAR e-files for individual filers and review them before transmission to FinCEN.

Follow these steps to create an FBAR e-file:

- **Complete and review your FBARs:**
- Complete and review your FBARs within a return. You can prepare only 1 FBAR in a return, except for 1040 returns.

  * For Form 1040, you can prepare separate FBARs for the taxpayer and spouse.
  * You can include multiple financial accounts on a single FBAR.
  * You need to prepare FBARs for **Individual Filers** within Form 1040 returns.
- **Generate a validation file:**
- Run a full recompute of the return, then generate a validation file.
- In the e-file folder of the **FBAR Organizer**, generate the validation file.

  note

  The validation process detects errors and omissions so you don't have to program an extensive list of reject diagnostics.
- **Review and correct validation errors:**
- With the XML file generated for validation, go to 

  **View****Diagnostics****Efile XML Validations Errors****FBAR**

   for a list of errors.
- Review each error, which explains the specific item you need to complete. Select the error and the system takes you to the field in the FBAR for correction.
- Repeat this process until you've eliminated all errors.
- **For Form 1040 returns only:** If you prepared separate FBARs for the taxpayer and spouse, you also need to generate separate validation files.

  note

  The validation errors at 

  **View****Diagnostics**

   only show errors from the last generated validation file. We recommend generating a validation file and correcting errors for 1 FBAR before validating the 2nd FBAR.
- **Create and review the FBAR e-file:**
- Create the FBAR e-file in the **e-file** folder of the **FBAR Organizer**.
- Review it using the **e-file Viewer**.

  The **e-file Viewer** shows the contents of the FBAR. While the system transmits a text-based file to FinCEN, the e-file Viewer shows information as an XML file. You can also view the FBAR information as a PDF file.
- **For Form 1040 Returns only:** If you prepared separate FBARs for the taxpayer and spouse, create separate FBAR e-files. The e-file Viewer displays both the taxpayer and spouse FBARs as separate files.

articles.title: E-file Form 990
articles.body_md:
# E-file Form 990

Set up, validate, and submit Form 990-series returns electronically to the IRS, then monitor their status.

- **Turn on e-file for your return**
- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Return****Enable E-file**

  .
- Enter your **EFIN**.
- Select **Type of Originator**.
- Select **Enable federal e-file**.
- Go to **Signature Authorization**.
- Select **State Options**.
- Go to **Signature Authorization** again.
- **Validate and correct errors**
- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Error Checking**

  .
- Select **Generate Validation Error**.
- When the process completes, go to 

  **View****Diagnostics**

  .
- Review items related to **Electronic Filing**.
- Review return information causing the diagnostic and make any changes to correct the data entry.
- Perform a full recompute and review any new e-file diagnostics.
- Modify your entries as needed.
- Repeat the modification, compute, and review process until no e-file diagnostics appear.
- **Create the e-file**
- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Return****Create E-file**

  .
- Select **Create Federal E-file 990/990EZ/990PF**.
- Check the **E-file Status** column for 1 of these messages:

  * **XML file is created - Return is 'Qualified'** (no errors)
  * **XML is created but NOT qualified - Diag needs to be cleared** (errors exist)
  * **XML is created but NOT qualified - Please clear all vali.errors** (validation errors exist)
- **Submit the e-file to the IRS**
- When you're ready to send qualified e-files to the IRS, go to 

  **RS Browser****Returns Processing****E-file****Select Returns**

  .

  note

  You must have ELF admin permissions to batch returns. If you don't have these options, see your firm administrator.
- Select the account, tax year, and tax type.
- Select **Return** as the **e-File Type**.
- Select **Continue**.
- Select whether the returns are **Federal Ready to Send** and/or **States/Cities read to send: All States/Cities**.
- Select **Continue** again.
- Select **Submit for e-file**.

**Check status and handle rejections**

The system will process and send your returns to the IRS. The status will show **Awaiting Acknowledgment** until the IRS approves or rejects the return.

To check the status, go to 

**RS Browser****Returns Processing****E-file****Status Report**

.

If the IRS rejects your return, open the locator, modify the erroneous information, recreate the e-file, and resubmit. All extension e-files have a 5-day perfection period (including weekends and holidays).

# 5500 filings excluded from e-filing

Find out which employee benefit filings are not eligible for electronic filing.

You can't e-file the following employee benefit filings:

* Filings sent using an application not approved by the DOL for e-file.
* Filings with accounting periods of more than 365 or (or 366 days for leap years).
* Filings that combine e-file and paper submissions.
* Filings with sections filed at different times instead of together.
* Filings submitted on unsupported media.
* Filings with unsupported attachment types.
* Unsigned filings (missing PIN and Signer ID for electronic signature).
* Unencrypted filings submitted via modern-to-modern or transmission.

Import filings prepared in EFAST2-approved third-party applications into IFILE and transmit them to the Department of Labor.

- Once you import the filing, you can add attachments to IFILE.

  * Accountant's Opinion: Must be a PDF document
  * Other attachments: PDF or plain text documents
  * No other formats are permitted

articles.title: Understand EFAST2 for 550 return e-filing
articles.body_md:
# Understand EFAST2 for 550 return e-filing

Learn about the Department of Labor's EFAST2 system, including user roles, credentials, and acknowledgment identifiers for filing Form 5500 returns.

The Department of Labor (DOL) requires you to e-file 5500 returns through its EFAST2 system.

All signers must obtain EFAST2 electronic credentials (user ID and PIN) to sign or submit Forms 5500 or 5500-SF.

## EFAST2 roles and user types

Before you register as an EFAST2 user, determine which filing tasks you need to perform, such as Filing Author, Signer, or Transmitter. This ensures you get the proper credentials. Your user type in EFAST2 depends on the system functions you need and your signature authority.

* **Filing Author**: Completes and submits Form 5500/5500-SF/5500-EZ and schedules. Can't sign unless also registered as a Filing Signer. You don't need this role if you use a third-party application.
* **Filing Signer**: Electronically signs Form 5500/5500-SF/5500-EZ. This includes Plan Administrators, Sponsors, and authorized service providers. Can't perform other filing functions alone.
* **Schedule Author**: Completes schedules for Form 5500/5500-SF/5500-EZ. Must export schedules for Filing Author to import. Can't initiate, sign, or submit filings.

## AckID

An Acknowledgment ID (AckID) is a unique identifier that the system generates when it successfully processes your submission. If you need to update a filing you made through EFAST2, include the original AckID.

articles.body_md:
# Submit a 1040 return for e-filing

Submit a completed 1040 return electronically to the IRS for faster processing and confirmation of receipt.

Before you begin, make sure you have:

* A completed 1040 return ready to file
* Your Electronic Filing Identification Number (EFIN)
* ELF administrator permissions to batch returns
* Taxpayer authorization to e-file

Use this procedure when you're ready to submit a 1040 return electronically to the IRS. E-filing provides faster processing and confirmation of receipt compared to paper filing.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Enable/Create**

  .
- Select the **Return** worksheet and turn on **Federal**.
- Enter your **EFIN**.
- Go to **Signature Authorization**.
- Select your signature option:

  * **Form 8879 - Practitioner PIN**
  * **Self-select PIN**
- Select who entered the PIN.

  important

  If you select **Taxpayer/spouse** and **Self-select PIN**, Form 8879 won't print. Keep the signed Form 8879 for 3 years and don't send it to the IRS.
- Enter the PINs and the date you entered them into the system.
- Go to 

  **Organizer****E-file****Error Checking**

  .
- Select **Generate Validation File**.
- When the process completes, go to 

  **View****Diagnostics**

  .
- Review items related to **Electronic Filing** and correct any data entry errors.
- Perform a full recompute and review any new e-file diagnostics.

  Repeat this step until no e-file diagnostics appear.
- Check the **E-file Status** column to make sure your return is ready.

  The status shows one of the following messages:

  * ```
    XML file is created - Return is 'Qualified means the e-file created without errors.

articles.title: Resolve e-file diagnostics
articles.body_md:
# Resolve e-file diagnostics

Learn about the 3 types of e-file diagnostics and how to review and correct errors before transmitting returns to the IRS.

The system generates 3 types of diagnostics to help you identify and correct issues before transmission:

* **E-file rejects:** These diagnostics identify conditions that will cause the IRS to reject your return if you transmit it. Correct all reject diagnostics before transmitting the file. Rejects typically flag missing information, mismatched data, or incorrect entries.
* **E-file alerts:** Alert diagnostics won’t prevent you from e-filing the return. However, you should still investigate these conditions, as they may reveal data entry errors that could cause problems later.
* **XML validation errors:** The system generates these errors only after it creates the XML file. The IRS determines the conditions that trigger validation errors, which generally relate to data formatting issues and unexpected information.

Follow these steps to review and correct e-file diagnostics:

- Select **View**, then **Diagnostics**.
- You will see 2 folders: **Types** and **Jurisdictions**.
- Expand each folder to view the diagnostics.
- Select each diagnostic to go directly to the condition that created it (if necessary).
- Make the necessary changes in the Organizer.
- Run a full recompute to verify you have resolved all issues.

articles.title: How electronic postmarks determine filing time
breadcrumb: How electronic postmarks determine filing time
articles.body_md:
# How electronic postmarks determine filing time

Learn how Thomson Reuters creates electronic postmarks and how the IRS adjusts them to the taxpayer's time zone to determine timely filing.

## Electronic postmark creation

Thomson Reuters creates an electronic postmark bearing the date and time (CT) that the e-file is received at our host computers. If a question arises about timeliness of filing, the IRS uses the electronic postmark adjusted to the taxpayer's time zone.

## Time zone adjustments

The IRS adjusts the electronic postmark based on the taxpayer's location:

* **Eastern Time** (ET): The IRS adds 1 hour to the electronic postmark to determine the filing time.
* **Pacific Time** (PT): The IRS subtracts 2 hours from the electronic postmark to determine the filing time.

## Plan for timely filing

To ensure you receive a timely electronic postmark, plan for possible transmission issues when you submit returns and extensions.

articles.title: IRS MeF system shutdown for tax year 2025 filing season
breadcrumb: IRS MeF system shutdown for tax year 2025 filing season
articles.body_md:
# IRS MeF system shutdown for tax year 2025 filing season

The IRS Modernized e-File (MeF) system will be unavailable from December 26, 2025 through mid-January 2026. Learn how to handle returns during this shutdown period.

## System shutdown details

The IRS will temporarily shut down the Modernized e-File (MeF) system to prepare for the Tax Year 2025 filing season. The shutdown affects:

* Individual returns: December 26, 2025 through early January 2026
* Business returns: December 26, 2025 through January 13, 2026
* All federal returns and state returns filed under the MeF federal/state program

## Filing options during shutdown

Don’t wait to file returns during the shutdown period. Consider paper filing if:

* The return has a balance due with accruing interest and penalties
* Credits or refunds may miss deadlines

## For tax preparers

If you are required to e-file returns, follow these steps when paper filing:

- Include Form 8948 with the paper return.
- Mark checkbox 6c.
- Enter the reason: 

  e-file was closed for the season

  .

## Thomson Reuters processing

Thomson Reuters won’t hold electronically filed returns during the shutdown. All electronic submissions will be rejected and must be filed on paper instead.

articles.title: Guidelines for attaching files to e-files
breadcrumb: Guidelines for attaching files to e-files
articles.body_md:
# Guidelines for attaching files to e-files

Follow IRS guidelines when attaching files with supporting documentation to e-filed tax returns.

## Attachment formats

You may need to attach supporting documentation to e-files, including tax forms, statements, elections, notices, schedules, or other information the IRS requires through form instructions, regulations, or publications. You can submit attachments electronically as XML documents or PDF files.

## XML documents

The IRS has defined schemas for the following information that you must provide in XML format:

* **Tax forms**: The system automatically formats tax form information included in the return as XML.
* **Supporting information**: Tax form instructions often request information to support specific lines, such as other income. The system automatically formats this additional return information into XML. The schema may provide specific data elements or allow free-form text.
* **Regulatory information**: Information requested in regulations or publications not specified in form instructions.

note

If information for either attachment type requires columnar format, the IRS lets you include it as a PDF attachment.

## PDF attachments

Tax returns may also include non-XML documents, known as binary attachments, submitted in PDF format. PDF attachments let you submit requested documentation, including signatures and third-party documents.

You can create PDF files using any available tool, but follow these IRS guidelines:

* Use Adobe Acrobat version 7 or newer to optimize file size when creating PDF attachments
* For scanned documents, move the compression/quality slider on the **Create PDF From Scanner** tool to increase compression and lower file size
* Keep each uncompressed PDF under 60 MB. All uncompressed PDFs in the return can't exceed 1 GB combined
* Limit PDF file names to 57 characters for 1040 returns and 23 characters for 1065 returns, including the file extension
* Avoid these special characters in file names and descriptions:


  + Single and double quotation marks (**' "**)
  + Angle brackets (**< >**)
  + Ampersand (**&**)
  + Exclamation mark (**!**)

When attaching a PDF, enter a meaningful description of 128 characters or less. For art appraisals, the IRS requires the description to begin with “Art Appraisal.”

articles.title: General dependency schema for e-filing
articles.body_md:
# General dependency schema for e-filing

Learn about IRS-defined general dependency types and their required data elements when submitting information outside predefined schemas.

The general dependency schema lets you submit information that doesn't fit into a predefined schema. You can enter general dependencies by going to 

**Organizer****E-file****Attachments****General Dependency****Overview**

.

The IRS has defined 2 types of general dependencies for tax returns:

* General dependency (medium) is attached at the return level and can have an explanation up to 100,000 characters.
* General dependency (small) is attached at the form or schedule level. It can have an explanation up to 5,000 characters.

## General dependency types

The IRS defines 2 types of general dependencies for tax returns:

* **General dependency (medium):** Attaches at the return level and supports explanations up to 100,000 characters
* **General dependency (small):** Attaches at the form or schedule level and supports explanations up to 5,000 characters

## Required data elements

Each general dependency schema requires the following data elements:

* Business or person name.
* Taxpayer identification number.
* Form line or instruction reference and regulation reference.
* Description: Provide a meaningful title or explanation for the attachment. The IRS uses this as the general dependency title when viewing the return.
* Attachment information.

breadcrumb: Submit the required forms after e-file acceptance
articles.body_md:
# Submit the required forms after e-file acceptance

Complete the e-filing process by mailing Form 8453 and other required documents to the IRS after receiving acceptance of your Form 1040 e-file.

Before you begin:

* Make sure that the IRS has accepted the 1040 e-filed return.
* Have the e-file status report available.

Perform these tasks on the next working day after receiving the filing acceptance.

- Obtain the submission ID from the E-File Status Report.
- Transfer the submission ID to the correct form (8453, 8879, or 9325).
- Attach all required forms, schedules, and statements to Form 8453.
- Mail Form 8453 to the IRS service center within 3 business days of receiving acknowledgment.
- If there is a balance due without electronic debit, mail Form 1040-V with a check to the IRS.

The IRS receives all required forms and any balance due associated with the accepted 1040 return.

Identify the federal attachments required when filing a Form 1065 partnership return with each state or local jurisdiction.

Show all hidden content

The following list identifies the federal attachments required to accompany the state return for each state or locality.

Alabama

* Complete federal return including all federal K-1s, statements, and attachments
* A list of all omitted schedules must be provided, if requested

* Form 1065: Pages 1–5

Arizona

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

California

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Colorado

* No federal attachments required

Connecticut

* Form 1065, pages 1–5, without Schedule K-1s
* Taxpayers completing Form CT-1065/CT-1120SI — Connecticut Composite Income Tax Return are now required to attach copies of federal Form 1065 to paper-filed returns only
* Don’t attach copies of Schedule K-1s

Delaware

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

District of Columbia

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

District of Columbia UBT

* No federal attachments required

Florida

* No federal attachments required

Florida LLC

* No federal attachments required

Georgia

* Complete federal return including supporting schedules

Hawaii

* No federal attachments required

Idaho

* No federal attachments required

Illinois

* Don’t submit PDF file formats as a federal attachment
* Only federal Form 1065 forms and schedules are currently accepted

Indiana

* No federal attachments required

Iowa

* No federal attachments required

Kentucky

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Kentucky Cities: Fayette County

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Kentucky Cities: Lexington-Fayette Urban County

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Kentucky Cities: Louisville

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5

Louisiana

* No federal attachments required

Maine

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5

Maryland
