* Maryland Schedules K-1 must be attached when the Pass-Through Entity (PTE) is the recipient of a credit for which the PTE must account (for example, the PTE was a nonresident entity and had taxes paid on its behalf, or was a member of another PTE that was entitled to pass on a tax credit to its members). This includes all Form 510, Schedules B, and any Schedule K-1s showing credits earned by PTE.

Massachusetts

* No federal attachments required

Michigan

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5

Minnesota

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Mississippi

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Missouri

* If you select No on questions 1 and 2 on Form MO-1065, attach a copy of federal Form 1065 and all its schedules, including Schedule K-1
* If you select Yes on question 2 on Form MO-1065, attach a copy of federal Form 1065 and all its schedules, including Schedule K-1

* Schedule K-1 only

* Schedule K
* Schedule A

Montana

  + All Forms 1099
  + Form PR-1
  + Supporting Montana schedules (including K-1s)

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules
* Schedule K-1s

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

New Jersey

* No federal attachments required

New Mexico

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5

New York

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

New York City

* No federal attachments required

New York IT-204LL

* No federal attachments required

North Carolina

* Don’t attach a copy of federal Form 1065 or copies of K-1s to Form D-403
* If copies are needed, the state Department of Revenue will request them later

North Dakota

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5
* Schedule K-1

Ohio

* Schedule K-1

Ohio Cities: CCA

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Ohio Cities: Cincinnati

* Form 1065, Pages 1–5
* Schedule K-1 (all)

Ohio Cities: RITA

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Oklahoma

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Oregon

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules
* Form 1065-B, including statements and schedules

Pennsylvania

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Pennsylvania Cities: Philadelphia

* Don’t staple, fold, or submit photocopies of the tax return
* Don’t submit copies of federal returns
* File only required schedules

Rhode Island

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

South Carolina

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Tennessee

* No federal attachments required

Texas

* No federal attachments required

Utah

* No federal attachments required

Vermont

* Form BI-471
* Form 1065, Pages 1–5
* All supporting Vermont schedules and statements

Virginia

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

West Virginia

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

Wisconsin

* Complete federal return including statements and schedules

# Form 1120 federal attachments required by state

Identify the federal attachments required when filing a Form 1120 return with each state or local jurisdiction.

Show all hidden content.

The following list identifies the federal attachments required to accompany the state return for each state or locality.

Alabama

* Signed copy of the federal return (Form 1120, 1120S or 1120F) as filed with the IRS, with the necessary supporting schedules, forms, and statements:
* Schedule D
* Schedule UTP
* Form 8886
* Form 4797
* Balance sheet
* Supporting statements for other income and other deductions
* Refer to form instructions for specific requirements by Alabama return type.

Alaska

* A complete federal corporate return is required, including statements and schedules.
* Attach a complete copy of the signed federal income tax return.
* If the federal return was part of a consolidated return, a copy of the consolidated federal return in which the taxpayer was included must be submitted.
* Affiliated taxpayers electing to file an Alaska consolidated return must include a complete copy of each federal income tax return of those corporations filing the Alaska return. A proforma return will NOT fulfill this requirement.
* If the federal return exceeds 50 pages, in lieu of the entire federal return, attach:


  + A copy of Pages 1 through 5 of federal Forms 1120, 1120S, 1120F, along with copies of the schedules and attachments filed in response to questions 3 and 5 of Form 1120, Schedule K.
  + Schedule D and supporting schedules.
  + If credits are claimed on the Alaska return, copies of Form 3800, along with supporting federal forms and schedules for each credit reported on Form 3800.
  + Form 4626 with supporting schedules and attachments, as well as Form 8827 with supporting schedules and attachments, if required.
  + Form 7004, if required.
  + If a consolidated federal return is filed, copies of the schedules prepared for the computation of consolidated taxable income. The schedules must show the separate taxable incomes for each member of the federal consolidated group with the consolidating eliminations and adjustments made to arrive at consolidated taxable income.
  + Form 851 and supporting schedules.
  + Form 2220 and supporting schedules.
  + Form 4797 and supporting schedules.
  + Signed copy of Form 8453, if e-filed.

Arizona

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Arkansas

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

California

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Colorado

* No federal attachments required.
* If the taxpayer has IRC 965 income, they must submit a copy of their IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement with their Colorado income tax return.

Connecticut

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Delaware

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Attach a completed copy of the federal return, including all schedules and attachments.
* Each member of an affiliated group must also attach a spreadsheet of all items of income and deduction reconciling the separate items of each member corporation to the consolidated totals.
* Form 1118, if required.
* Form 5884, Jobs Credit, if required.
* A copy of federal Form 1139 to any Claim for Refund of Delaware corporation income taxes, if required.

District of Columbia

* Some forms and schedules are required.
* if required, attach federal Form 4562, Schedule M-3, Form 4797, Schedule D, and any other forms or schedules necessary to process the return.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Florida

* Some forms and schedules are required.
* Corporations must attach one of the following to Florida Form F-1120:


  + A copy of the actual federal income tax return filed with the IRS.
  + Schedule M-3, and any supporting details for Schedules M-1 and M-2.
  + Form 4562.
  + Form 851, if Florida F-851 is not included.
  + Form 1122, if required.
  + Form 1125-A, if required.
  + Form 4626, if required.
  + Schedule D, if required.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Georgia

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Attach federal forms, such as 1120, 1120S, and supporting forms and schedules, including Form 4562.

Hawaii

* No federal attachments required.
* If Form 3115 is being filed with the IRS, attach a copy to the 1st Hawaii return affected by the change.
* For taxpayers claiming federal “bonus” depreciation, attach a federal Form 4562 for Hawaii tax purposes.
* If the corporation used the look-back method under section 460(b)(2) for certain long-term contracts and an amount is due, attach federal Form 8697.

Idaho

* Idaho returns included in the Federal/State Electronic Filing (MeF) Program will be transmitted to the IRS Service Center along with the federal return.
* All Idaho returns must include a complete copy of the federal return to include all PDF attachments, forms, and schedules.
* Once the IRS has notified the Electronic Return Originator (ERO) of successful submission, Idaho can retrieve the files from the IRS.
* Idaho won't receive any state data from a rejected federal return.
* Note: The IRS acknowledges only that it received the state data. The IRS acknowledgment isn't an indication that Idaho has “received” your state return. You must receive the Idaho acknowledgment to ensure your state return has been received.

Illinois

* Don’t submit PDF file formats as federal attachment.
* Only federal 1120 and 1120S forms and schedules are currently accepted.

Indiana

* Main federal form — all pages.
* Form 1118 duplicate.
* Form 7004 duplicate.
* Schedule M-3.

Iowa

* A copy of the entire federal submission, formatted in XML according to the relevant IRS schema.

Kentucky

* Form 1120, all pages.
* Or, if Form 1120 is not filed, attach copies of the income statement, cost of goods sold schedule, and balance sheet of the federal form filed.
* Or, if the corporation is not required to submit a balance sheet for federal income tax purposes, attach the balance sheet prepared on a consistent basis from the books and records of the corporation.
* Form 1125-A.
* Form 1125-E.
* Form 851.
* Form 4797.
* Schedule D.
* Form 5884.
* Schedule L with state attached schedule.
* Form 3800.

Kentucky Cities: Lexington-Fayette Urban County

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* We supply some of the federal attachments required.

Kentucky Cities: Louisville

* Some forms and schedules are required:


  + Form 1120.
  + Form 1120S, Page 1.
  + Form 1120S, Page 2 — Schedule of Other Deductions.
  + Form 8825 and supporting rental schedules.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Louisiana

* No federal attachments required.

Maine

* Some forms and schedules are required.
* Maine requires C Corporations to attach the following to the state return:


  + 1120 federal return, Pages 1-5.
  + Schedule M-3.
  + Schedule D.
  + Form 4562.
  + Form 4626.
  + Form 4797.
* S Corporations must attach:


  + Form 1120S, Pages 1-4.
  + Schedule D.
  + Form 4562.
  + Form 4797.
  + Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
* If the corporation is a member of a federal consolidation, attach:


  + Federal return.
  + Consolidated Form 1120, Pages 1-5.

Maryland

* Some forms and schedules are required.
* Attach a copy of Pages 1-5 of federal Form 1120 to MD Form 500.
* Corporations included in a consolidated filing for federal income tax purposes must file separate returns for Maryland purposes and attach a copy of Pages 1-5 of the consolidated federal return to each Maryland filing.
* The filing should also include a copy of the columnar schedules of income/expenses or balance sheet items required for the federal filing that reconcile the separate items of each member corporation to the consolidated totals.

Massachusetts

* No federal attachments required.
* Corporations must make an exact copy of the federal form, including any required schedules, forms, and any other documentation required to substantiate entries made on the state return, available to the Department of Revenue upon request.

Michigan

* Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
* Schedule D.
* Form 851.
* Form 4562.
* Form 4797.
* If the filing is part of a consolidated federal return, attach a proforma return or a consolidation schedule.

Michigan Cities: Common Forms

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Michigan Cities: Detroit

* Copy of federal 1120 or 1120S, including Schedule K-1, to support the amount on line 1a.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Minnesota

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Any additional information requested.
* Copy of all returns filed with the IRS for the tax year, including 1120-FSCs.
* Copies of all supporting schedules, except for Forms 1118, 1122, 3115, 5471, 5472, and 5713.

Mississippi

* Combined filers must attach:


  + Consolidated Federal Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
  + Schedule M-3 and a complete proforma federal return.
  + Form 8873.
  + Form 7004.
  + A signed copy of federal Form 990-T.
* Taxpayers who elect the installment method for federal income tax purposes should include:


  + Form 6252.
  + Schedule of any differences between the federal and Mississippi amounts.
  + Form 4562 must be completed twice and attached immediately after Form 83-122.

Missouri

* Some forms and schedules are required.
* Corporations must attach:


  + Copy of federal Form 1120, Pages 1-5, or Pages 1-4 for S Corporations.
  + Schedule M-3.
* S Corporations must also attach all Schedule K-1s and Form 8886.
* We don’t support attachments for consolidated federal/separate Missouri return filers, who must include consolidated federal Form 1120, Schedule J, Form 8886, and an income statement or summary of profit companies.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of the 2018 release.

Missouri Cities: Kansas City

* Federal tax return or Schedule K-1.

Missouri Cities: St. Louis

* The 1st page of the federal tax return.
* Schedule K Distributive Share Items for 1120S.
* Form 1125-A Cost of Goods Sold.
* Any statements that substantiate the deductions of these forms.
* Schedules L, M-1, and M-2.

Montana

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* If the federal return is voluminous:


  + Pages 1-5 of the return along with specified schedules.
  + Schedule M-3.
  + Schedule N.
  + Schedule UTP.
* Members of a federal consolidated group or combined reporting group must attach Pages 1-5 of the ultimate parent company's consolidated federal return.
* if required:


  + Form 2220.
  + Form 3468.
  + Form 4797.
  + Form 5471.

Nebraska

* Federal return and supporting schedules.
* At a minimum:


  + A copy of the 1st 5 pages.
  + Schedule D.
  + Form 4797.
  + Supporting schedules of Form 1120.
* If a consolidated federal return is filed, attach a copy of the consolidating schedules or workpapers for:


  + Income and expenses.
  + Cost of goods sold.
  + Balance sheets.
* Form 851.
* Copies of schedules and other information, which support the numbers reported on Nebraska return.
* Form 7004.
* Form 2220.
* Form 1118, Parts A, and B.
* A proforma federal return is not acceptable.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

New Hampshire

* Pages 1 through 5 of the federal return, including all relevant schedules supporting the amounts reported on the federal return, should be attached.

New Jersey

* No federal attachments required.
* User can copy any federal form, attach it to the NJ return, and mail it to the state.
* If the taxpayer files federal Schedule M-3, Schedule C must be filed, and a copy of federal M-3 must be attached to the NJ CBT-100 return.
* If the taxpayer is part of a consolidated filing, then federal Schedule M-3 must be on a separate entity basis.
* A corporation included in a consolidated federal income tax return must complete all schedules on its own separate basis and attach a copy of Form 851, filed with Form 1120 for federal income tax purposes.

New Mexico

* Federal return, Pages 1-5.
* Corporations filing under separate corporate entity or combined filing methods must attach simulated/proforma Form 1120, Pages 1-5.

New York

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Form CT-3.
* Form CT-4, simplified form.
* Members of a federal affiliated group that files a consolidated return, where the state combined group is the same as the federal group, or all members of the state group are included in a larger federal group filing the consolidated return, must attach:


  + Federal consolidated return and consolidating workpapers.
  + Forms 8886 if Form DTF-686 is included in the return.
* If the federal return is part of a consolidation:


  + Proforma federal return.

New York City

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

North Carolina

* Corporations filing federal Schedule M-3 must attach a copy of the completed schedule to the North Carolina corporate income tax return.
* Filers of a consolidated group must attach a separate copy of the proforma federal return.
* Entire return must be made available to NC DOR upon request.

North Dakota

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Form 7004, if required, must be attached.

Ohio

* Attach a paper copy of the federal extension or provide the federal confirmation number if the federal extension was filed electronically to receive an Ohio extension to the federal extension due date if that date is beyond the unextended Ohio due date for either Form IT 1140 or Form IT 4708.
* Also check the federal extension field on IT 1140 or IT 4708.

Ohio Cities: CCA

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Ohio Cities: Cincinnati

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Ohio Cities: Columbus

* Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
* Form 1120S, Pages 1-4.
* Schedule K-1, all.

Ohio Cities: RITA

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

Oklahoma

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Special instructions regarding OK Form 512, Page 4: instructions state to complete Page 4 or attach a copy of federal Form 1120, Schedules L, M-1, and M-2.
* Corporations that are not required to complete federal Form 1120, Schedules L, M-1, and M-2 are still required to complete Oklahoma Form 512, Page 4 — Balance Sheets, Reconciliation of Income per Books with Income per Return, OK M-1, and Analysis of Unappropriated Return Earnings per Books, OK M-2.
* Corporations that are not required to complete federal Form 1120, Schedule M-1 due to the requirement to complete Schedule M-3 must either complete the Oklahoma Schedule M-1, or enclose a copy of federal Schedule M-3.

Oregon

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Form 7004.
* Oregon Form 20-INS doesn’t require a federal copy attachment.

Oregon Cities/Counties: Portland

* No federal attachments required.

Pennsylvania

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* Corporations must attach a copy of federal return, such as Forms 1120, 1120S, 1065, and so forth.
* If included in a consolidated federal report, you must file:


  + Income statement reflecting taxable income that would have been listed on a separate federal return.
  + A balance sheet reflecting the financial position of the corporation at the beginning and end of the taxable year as would have been listed on a separate federal return.
  + Schedules on Pages 2, 3, 4, and 5 of Form 1120 as they would appear for a separate report.

Pennsylvania Cities: Philadelphia

* No federal attachments required.

Rhode Island

* Corporations must attach all required schedules from federal Form 1120 to the Rhode Island business corporation tax return.
* Print capability has been added for foreign corporations.

South Carolina

* Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
* We supply all federal attachments required as of 2017 release.

Tennessee

* No attachments required, but at the commissioner's discretion, any taxpayer might be required to file a copy of the federal tax forms for the same tax year with its Tennessee franchise/excise tax return.

Texas

* No federal attachments required.

Utah

* Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
* Schedule M-3 and IRS Form 1125-A, if required.
* Other detail schedules are not required to be included unless otherwise specified by the Tax Commission, but they can be requested by the Audit Division later.

Vermont: C Corp

* Form 1120, Pages 1-5, or other return filed.
* One form is required if the consolidated group is the same as the Vermont unitary group, or one for each separate member if the affiliates are not part of the same federal consolidated group.
* If the consolidated/combined group is different from the federal group, this will be a proforma return.
* Form 4562 as filed and proforma if any members of the group have taken “bonus” depreciation.
* Copies of federal statements regarding other income and deductions, net operating loss, and taxes and licenses.

Vermont: S Corp

* Form BI-471.
* The 1st 5 pages of the federal income tax return, 1120S.
* All supporting Vermont schedules and statements.

Virginia

* The 2012-2014 Appropriations Act requires corporations subject to the income tax filing requirements for Virginia Form 500 to file their returns and make their payments electronically beginning 1/1/2013.
* A copy of the complete federal return as required is attached automatically in the XML file.

West Virginia

* Form 1120, Pages 1-5, signed.
* If you attach a proforma federal income tax return, the following consolidated return data is also required:


  + Pages 1 through 5 of the consolidated federal return plus supporting schedules showing the consolidation of the income statement, balance sheet, eliminations, and adjustments.
  + Federal Form 851.
  + Signed statement explaining the differences, if any, between the income statement and balance sheet reported for federal consolidated filing and that reported for West Virginia purposes.
  + Schedule M-3, when applicable.
  + Federal Form 1118, when applicable.
* We supply some of the federal attachments required.

Wisconsin

* All corporations filing Forms 4, 5, or 5S must include a complete copy of their federal income tax return, including all supporting schedules.
* If the corporation is filing as a separate entity for Wisconsin purposes but is included in a consolidated return for federal purposes, you must also provide either a breakdown of the federal consolidated return amounts by company or a copy of the proforma federal return for each corporation in the consolidated group.
* Form 851.
* Form 8886.
* Schedule UTP.

  • Pages 1 through 5 of the federal return, including all relevant schedules supporting the amounts reported on the federal return, should be attached.

  • No federal attachments required.
  • User can copy any federal form, attach it to the NJ return, and mail it to the state.
  • If the taxpayer files federal Schedule M-3, Schedule C must be filed, and a copy of federal M-3 must be attached to the NJ CBT-100 return.
  • If the taxpayer is part of a consolidated filing, then federal Schedule M-3 must be on a separate entity basis.
  • A corporation included in a consolidated federal income tax return must complete all schedules on its own separate basis and attach a copy of Form 851, filed with Form 1120 for federal income tax purposes.
New Mexico
  • Federal return, Pages 1-5.
  • Corporations filing under separate corporate entity or combined filing methods must attach simulated/proforma Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
New York
  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
  • Form CT-3.
  • Form CT-4, simplified form.
  • Members of a federal affiliated group that files a consolidated return, where the state combined group is the same as the federal group, or all members of the state group are included in a larger federal group filing the consolidated return, must attach:
    • Federal consolidated return and consolidating workpapers.
    • Forms 8886 if Form DTF-686 is included in the return.
  • If the federal return is part of a consolidation:
    • Proforma federal return.
New York City
  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
North Carolina
  • Corporations filing federal Schedule M-3 must attach a copy of the completed schedule to the North Carolina corporate income tax return.
  • Filers of a consolidated group must attach a separate copy of the proforma federal return.
  • Entire return must be made available to NC DOR upon request.
North Dakota
  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
  • Form 7004, if required, must be attached.
Ohio
  • Attach a paper copy of the federal extension or provide the federal confirmation number if the federal extension was filed electronically to receive an Ohio extension to the federal extension due date if that date is beyond the unextended Ohio due date for either Form IT 1140 or Form IT 4708.

  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
Ohio Cities: Cincinnati
  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
Ohio Cities: Columbus
  • Form 1120, Pages 1-5.
  • Form 1120S, Pages 1-4.
  • Schedule K-1, all.
Ohio Cities: RITA
  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
  • Special instructions regarding OK Form 512, Page 4: instructions state to complete Page 4 or attach a copy of federal Form 1120, Schedules L, M-1, and M-2.

  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.
  • Form 7004.

Oregon Cities/Counties: Portland
  • No federal attachments required.

  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

  • No federal attachments required.

  • Complete federal form, including statements and schedules.

  • No federal attachments required.

articles.body_md:
# Attach a PDF to an e-file

Add and review PDF attachments for e-filed returns.

Follow these steps to attach a PDF:

- With the return open, select **Edit**, **Insert**, then **EFile Attachments**.
- Select **Add**.
- Select the jurisdiction or form.
- Select **Browse**, then select the PDF you want to attach.
- Select **Next**.
- Select a predefined title or enter your own. The default user-defined title is the file name, without the extension.

  important

  When you select the PDF, the system automatically populates the description with the PDF file name. If necessary, change the description to an IRS-accepted name. Make sure the attachment file name matches the IRS-required descriptions. For attachments not listed in the IRS specifications, use meaningful and descriptive names. Your actual file name becomes the description of the attachment and can't exceed 100 characters.

  note

  You can't change the Thomson Reuters file name and date modified.
- Select **Next**.

  The system displays the selected PDF with the jurisdiction, attachment title, file name, file size, and date modified in the 

  E-file Attachments

   window.
- Select **Done** to complete the attachment.

Select **E-file**, then **Attachments** on the 

Organizer

 screen to review the PDF attachments included in the return.

articles.title: Delete trapped PDF attachments
articles.body_md:
# Delete trapped PDF attachments

Clear PDF attachments that appear in the Organizer's summary but don't show when you try to attach them.

Follow these steps to delete trapped attachments:

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Federal E-file****Attachments****PDF Attachments****Summary**

  .
- Select **Attach PDF**.
- Add any document as a PDF to this return.
- Close the 

  PDF Attachment

   window.
- Select **Attach PDF** again to re-open the window.
- Delete the PDF you attached and close the window.
- Perform a full recompute.

The trapped PDF attachments should now be gone.

articles.title: Error: The file you attempted to upload doesn’t meet minimum file requirements (fillable form)
breadcrumb: Error: The file you attempted to upload doesn’t meet minimum file requirements (fillable form)
articles.body_md:
# Error: The file you attempted to upload doesn’t meet minimum file requirements (fillable form)

Resolve the minimum file requirements error that occurs when you upload fillable form PDFs to an e-file.

## Scenario

When you attempt to attach a fillable form PDF file to an e-file, you may receive this error message:

**Error message**

```
The file you attempted to upload does not meet minimum file requirements. Please correct the file and try again.
```

## Solution

Fillable form PDF files must be saved as a standard PDF before you can attach them to an e-file.

- Open the PDF you're attempting to attach.
- Select **Print**.
- Select **Microsoft Print to PDF** or **Save as PDF**.
- Select **Print** and save the PDF to your computer.
- Reattach the PDF and the e-file attachment.

articles.title: Error: Document has fillable forms
articles.body_md:
# Error: Document has fillable forms

Fix the “Unable to create PDF output” error that occurs when you attach PDFs with fillable forms or password protection to e-file returns.

## Scenario

You may get the following error message when printing a return or selecting **Send to PDF**.

```
Error: Document has fillable forms, Unable to create PDF output.
```

## Cause

The Organizer doesn't currently support PDFs with fillable forms or password-protected PDFs as e-file attachments.

## Solution

- Find the PDF with fillable forms attached to the e-file.
- Select **Delete** to remove the PDF from the e-file.
- Open the PDF you're trying to attach.
- Select **Print**.
- From the **Printer** dropdown, select **Microsoft Print to PDF** (or **Save as PDF** if you opened the PDF from a browser).
- Select **Print** and save the flattened PDF to your computer.
- Attach the newly saved PDF to the e-file.
- Select **Print** or **Send to PDF**.

This process converts the fillable PDF into a standard PDF format that the Organizer can process.

articles.title: Set up and create an aggregated New York e-file
breadcrumb: Set up and create an aggregated New York e-file
articles.body_md:
# Set up and create an aggregated New York e-file

Configure and generate an aggregated New York e-file by attaching K-1 XML files from subsidiary returns to the primary return.

Follow these steps to set up and create an aggregated New York e-file:

- **Create and prepare the subsidiary return e-file.**
- In the subsidiary return, create the e-file. The New York e-file will have an extension of **XXXXXXXX.XNY**.
- Rename the New York e-file to 

  XXXXXXXXNY.XML

  .
- **Attach K-1 XML files to the primary return.**
- In the primary return, go to 

  **Organizer****States****New York****E-file****Attachments****K-1 Aggregation**

  .
- Select **NY K1 Aggregation**.
- Select **Attach K-1 Aggregation XML File**.
- Select **New York K-1 Aggregation** for **Attachment Jurisdiction**.
- Select **Browse** to find and select the XML file created earlier, then select **Upload** to attach it to the return.
- Select **Done**. Repeat steps 5-8 for each XML file you want to include.
- After you attach the XML files, verify their details are correct in the **K-1 Attachments Summary**.

  important

  The system validates attached XML files to detect XML errors. If validation errors exist, delete the attachment, correct the errors in the subsidiary return, recreate the XML file, and re-attach it.
- **Configure optional settings.**
- (Optional) If you don't want to include the beneficiary information from the primary return in the XML file, select **Suppress system generated Form IT-205, Schedule C**.
- On the **New York K1 Aggregation** page in the primary return, override the total number of beneficiaries if needed. The system includes this number in the total number of beneficiaries in the aggregated XML file.
- **Create the aggregated e-file.**
- Go to **Organizer** **E-file** **Enable/Create** for the primary return.
- In the **Enable** column, select **New York**.
- Select **Create Return E-file**.

articles.title: Merge third-party XML files with your international e-file
breadcrumb: Merge third-party XML files with your international e-file
articles.body_md:
# Merge third-party XML files with your international e-file

Upload third-party XML files to include international forms in your e-file submission and learn how to complete the merge process.

## Upload third-party XML files

When you upload or attach a third-party XML e-file, the system includes only the following international forms in the final XML file: Forms 926, 1118, 5471, 8621, 8858, and 8865. Ensure your third-party files use the XML file extension.

## Attach PDF files separately

The system doesn’t include PDF attachments from third-party e-files in the merge process. Instead, attach all PDF files separately by going to 

**Edit****Insert****E-file Attachments**

 in the browser.

## Complete Schedule N manually

The system doesn’t automatically update Schedule N Questions - Foreign Operations of U.S. Corporations with information from merged XML files. Manually update these questions in 

**Organizer****General Information****Miscellaneous Information****Schedule N Questions**

.

## Validate third-party files before merging

Validate your third-party XML file to detect XML errors before attempting to merge. If the third-party XML file contains validation errors, the system won't complete the merge process.

## Create the e-file

The Create Electronic File process merges third-party XML files with other XML files. This creates the final XML for IRS submission. You can merge third-party XML files only in single or top consolidation returns.

articles.title: Review and resolve e-file mismatches
articles.body_md:
# Review and resolve e-file mismatches

View the e-file summary to identify mismatches between locator amounts and e-file amounts, and resolve differences by recreating the e-file XML.

You can still submit the return for e-filing even if there are differences. The mismatch status alerts you that the system calculated the return with different key amounts after its last e-file XML creation.

You can view the e-file summary in 2 places:

* **E-file Viewer**: Select the PDF folder to open the PDF in a separate window.
* **E-file Submission**: If the amounts match between the locator and the e-file, the e-file status displays as **Qualified**.

When amounts in the locator and e-file don't match, the e-file status shows **Qualified – Mismatch** instead of **Qualified**. This occurs when locator amounts change but you don't create a new e-file.

Select **Qualified – Mismatch** to display the **E-file Summary Report**. The system shows differences in red.

note

You can still submit the return for e-file if the e-file status is **Qualified Mismatch**. This only alerts you that the system computed the return with different key amounts after its last e-file XML creation.

To resolve any differences between the e-file and the tax return numbers, open the locator and re-create the e-file XML file.

articles.title: E-file viewer features and improvements
articles.body_md:
# E-file viewer features and improvements

The e-file viewer displays XML files as searchable PDFs with schema-based data, navigation features, and improved performance.

The e-file viewer displays your XML file contents as a PDF in Acrobat, organized according to IRS and state schemas. The viewer pulls identifying information directly from the schemas instead of using style sheets overlaid on tax form images.

**No dependence on IRS style sheets**

The e-file viewer doesn't rely on IRS-provided style sheets to display tax forms. Previously, the IRS didn't always provide style sheets on time, and they sometimes conflicted with the latest schemas. The system now pulls line numbers, descriptions, and element names directly from the current federal or state schemas, avoiding outdated style sheets.

**PDF format for all states**

In the past, reviewing a state e-file meant viewing raw XML because states didn't provide style sheets. The e-file viewer now uses a PDF format available for all states.

**Navigation features**

Each PDF includes the taxpayer name, FEIN, page number, and XML file creation date. Hyperlinks let you go to supporting documents like other forms or schedules. PDF bookmarks let you jump quickly to specific forms or details. When multiple forms or schedules are included, the number appears in parentheses, and you can expand the bookmark to see each one.

Use shortcut keys for navigation. For example, use **Alt + Left Arrow** to return to the previous view.

**Search capability**

Unlike style sheets, the PDF is searchable using the **Find** feature. You can search for element names from validation errors to understand the data context and help resolve validation issues.

**Performance improvements**

The e-file viewer performs faster, especially with large XML files. You no longer need to close the return to view the XML file or PDF. You can also save the PDF to your local machine.

articles.title: View e-file PDFs
articles.body_md:
# View e-file PDFs

Open the e-file viewer to view XML data with detailed line numbers and schema elements, and use the toolbar and bookmark features to review the PDF.

## Open the e-file viewer

Select the **PDF** folder to open the e-file viewer in a separate window. The PDF has detailed line numbers, describes schema elements, and shows XML data and schema element names.

note

The PDF doesn't show XML header information, such as taxpayer and paid preparer information. However, you can verify this information by reviewing the full XML file. To do this, select the file in the **PDF** folder.

## Use the toolbar

Once you open the e-file viewer, you can save or print the PDF file. You have 2 options for saving or printing:

* Using the PDF toolbar
* When the PDF file initializes

The toolbar also lets you:

* Send the PDF file in an email.
* Access a specific page directly and enter a number in the page field or use the arrows.
* Find content by entering a word or phrase in the word field.

## Use the e-file viewer

When you use the e-file viewer, the PDF grid opens in a separate window, displaying the PDF grid.

Each page of the PDF file shows:

* Taxpayer's name
* Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Social Security number (SSN)
* Timestamp when the PDF was created
* Page number

The viewer shows all schema elements, regardless of whether they contain data.

This bar includes the schema name, the document ID, and informational text (like the dormant indicator for Form 1040). It shows blue underlined hyperlinks. These links open supplemental schemas that the form calls but doesn't tie to a specific line number.

When schemas offer multiple elements, you can only select one. The system indents descriptions for each choice. For example, for **Method of Accounting** like “cash,” “accrual,” and “other” might apply, but you can only select 1.

The system shows items that can appear multiple times in consecutive order, with a header marking the beginning of each occurrence. For instance, you can include 2 separate items in **Dependent Information**.

Hyperlinks take you to supporting details. For example, if line 21 has details for **Other Income**, its description will include a hyperlink.

Select the hyperlink to view the supporting details. You can include the 1st item in **Other Income**.

## **Use the bookmark view**

The **Bookmark view** lists the form and schedule schemas within the PDF file.

- Select the icon circled in red to open the view.
- Select each form or schedule schema to go directly to that specific section in the PDF.
- Select the plus sign next to the file name. This expands the list and shows each file's unique identifier (such as IRS1040SchCN1, IRS1040SchCN2, IRS1040SchCN3).


  - When a form has multiple instances, a plus sign appears next to its file name.
  - A form like Schedule C might have multiple instances. The total number of forms appears in parentheses.
  - The form's initial instance has parentheses, while subsequent instances have "N1" or "N2" at the end.
- Select the bookmark to go to that specific instance of the form.

articles.title: Review the e-file status report
articles.body_md:
# Review the e-file status report

Use the jurisdiction hyperlink on the e-file Batch Status list to view the Cumulative History report, which details current and past e-file histories.

The **E-file Status Report** shows the status of e-filed returns and returns not yet ready for e-filing on a return-by-return basis across various stages.

Follow these steps to search for returns and jurisdictions on the **E-file Status Report**.

- Select **Reports**, then **E-file Status Report** to enter and select your search criteria and options.
- Make choices for either or both federal and states jurisdictions. Choices include:

  - **Ignore Federal or Ignore State**: Use this option to refine your search criteria and limit the time and volume of data the Status Report produces.
  - **Requested**: The taxing authority has acknowledged these jurisdictions but hasn't yet reviewed them.
  - **Awaiting Acknowledgment**: This option shows you which returns and jurisdictions the system has successfully transmitted to the taxing authority but the authority hasn't yet processed.
  - **Conditional Accepted**: The taxing authority has accepted the return with conditions.
  - **Accepted**: Select this option to list the returns and jurisdictions that the taxing authorities have successfully transmitted and accepted.
  - **Rejected**: Select this option for a list of jurisdictions that you have submitted to the correct taxing authority and that the authority has rejected.
  - **Fed rejected - state not processed**: If you submit the federal return and state return together, and the taxing authority rejects the federal return, the system won’t process the state return. The following 1040 states require you to file the federal return with the state return: Alabama (residents only), Arizona, Arkansas, Kansas, Michigan (only if federal 8879 is used), Mississippi, Oklahoma.
  - **Error - Not Submitted**: This status lists returns that encountered errors during the transmission of submitted jurisdictions. The system hasn’t submitted returns with this status to the jurisdiction and you will need to resubmit them.
  - **Ready to Send**: The report shows qualified jurisdictions not yet submitted when you select this option.
  - **Not Ready to Send**: This option shows you which returns and jurisdictions still have e-file diagnostics in the return's Organizer, or other disqualifications that prevent successful e-filing.
  - **All Statuses (excluding Ready to Send)**: This option shows you all returns submitted for e-file and the status for each jurisdiction within those returns.

**E-file Status Report** results:

* **Error Not Submitted**: For federal and state jurisdictions, for returns and extensions (all e-file types). This lists the submitted returns that can't complete the submission process.
* **Accepted**: Select the link on a listed jurisdiction abbreviation to display the Cumulative History report for the selected jurisdiction.
* **Ready to Send**: You can export this report to a PDF or Excel spreadsheet.
* **Not Ready to Send**: States only for All Tax Types.

articles.title: Retain e-file records and documents
articles.body_md:
# Retain e-file records and documents

Retain e-file records, acknowledgment files, and signature documents for the required time periods based on IRS requirements.

Retain this information until the end of the calendar year you filed the return, or until 9 months after the fiscal year of filing.

* A copy of the signed IRS e-file consent to disclosure forms for taxpayers who signed using a scanned signature form (Form 8453).
* A copy of the electronic portion of the return you converted into an e-file transmission for the IRS.
* The acknowledgment file for IRS accepted returns.
* The acknowledgment for all extensions.

Retain form 8879-PE for 3 years from the due date or IRS received date, whichever is later.

E-filers who originate their own returns need to retain all information that a taxpayer would retain for the time period.

Providers can image and store all paper records they must retain for IRS e-file. This includes signed signature documents and any supporting documents not included in the e-file. This storage system must satisfy the requirements of [Revenue Procedure 97-22, Retention of Books and Records](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/rp-97-22.pdf).

# E-file diagnostic: Balance or refund change

Recreate your e-file when the balance due or refund amount changes to ensure the electronic file matches the current return.

```
Electronic Filing: The balance due or refund changed since you last created an electronic file. Recreate the electronic file to match the current return.
```

## Solution

Recreate the e-file to ensure it contains the current balance due or refund amount and matches the return data.

note

This diagnostic may not disappear after recomputing. After you recreate the e-file, review and verify the return. Submit the return if the e-file is accurate.

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: Form 1310 Taxpayer
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Form 1310 Taxpayer

Learn how to resolve the Form 1310 e-file diagnostic error that occurs when selecting surviving spouse or court-appointed representative options for filing statuses other than married filing joint.

```
Form 1310 Taxpayer - Electronic Filing: The option for surviving spouse requesting reissuance of a refund or court-appointed or certified personal representative are not allowed when the filing status is not married filing joint.
```

## Cause

This diagnostic occurs because the IRS has tightened e-filing rules for decedent returns due to fraud concerns. For single decedent returns with a court-appointed representative selected, the return must be paper filed. The only allowable e-file option for a single individual is Option C on Form 1310: **Person, other than A or B, claiming refund for the decedent's estate**.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **Informational Forms** folder.
- Go to the **Deceased Refund**, **Taxpayer Deceased Refund** folder.
- Go to the **Tax payer**, **Deceased Refund** tab.
- In **PERSON CLAMING REFUND**, change the option to **B** or **C**.
- Clear the **Personal Representative** checkbox.
- Enter the information following this section.
- Run a full recompute, then recreate the e-file.

note

If option **A** is selected or if **Personal Representative** is selected, you'll need to file the return on paper.

breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Form 3800 - General Business Credit:
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Form 3800 - General Business Credit:

Learn how to resolve various Form 3800 e-file diagnostic errors that occur when required line items are missing values based on entries in other parts of the form.

One or more e-file diagnostics appear for Form 3800. Examples include:

```
Form 3800 - General Business Credit: If Part III, line 6, column (f) has a value and Part III Line 3, column (j) has a non-zero value, then Form 3800, Part II, line 24 must have a value.
```

```
Form 3800 – General Business Credit: If Part III Line 2, column (f) has a non-zero value, then Form 3800 Part I, line 3 must have a value.
```

This happens when there is an amount Form 3800 and the program is consequently expecting another line on Form 3800 to have a value.

## Cause

This diagnostic occurs when an amount is entered on Form 3800 and the program expects a corresponding value on another line of the form. Many amounts in Parts I and II auto-populate based on entries in Part III.

## Solution

Review the e-file diagnostic to identify which lines on Form 3800 are in question. Review the form instructions or consider overriding amounts if needed.

- Go to 

  **Tax Forms****Federal**

  .
- Select **Form 3800 - General Business Credit**, then go to the line items in question.
- If there are amounts present, go to the line referenced at the end of the diagnostic and make sure there is an amount or 

  NONE

   entered.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Form 8867 Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Form 8867 Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist

Learn how to complete the required Form 8867 Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist when claiming Child Tax Credit, Additional Child Tax Credit, or Credit for Other Dependents to avoid e-file errors and potential penalties.

```
Form 8867 Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist: You have taken the Child Tax Credit, Additional Child Tax Credit, or the Credit for Other Dependents but have not completed the required Form 8867. Go to Organizer / Credits / Child Tax Credit / Form 8867 / Paid Preparer Selection and generate a Form 8867 by selecting Yes under the include column for the applicable paid preparer that did the work on this credit. Then fill out the Form 8867 organizer that generates below the paid preparer selection screen. The penalty for failure to meet the due diligence requirements with respect to returns and claims for refund is $635 per credit per return.
```

## Cause

This diagnostic occurs when you have claimed a credit mentioned in the error but have not completed the required Form 8867 Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist.

## Solution

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Credits**

  .
- Go to the **Child Tax Credit** (or the credit you are taking), then the **Form 8867** folder.
- Go to the **Paid Preparer Selection** folder.
- In the **Include** column, select **Yes** for at least 1 preparer.
- When you select **Yes**, a folder will appear following **Paid Preparer Selection** with the name of the preparer you selected.
- In that folder, enter the information for **Form 8867**.
- Run a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: Form 1040, line 34 (overpayment amount) is greater than line 38
breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Form 1040, line 34 (overpayment amount) is greater than line 38
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Form 1040, line 34 (overpayment amount) is greater than line 38

```
Form 1040: If Form 1040, line 34 (overpayment amount) is greater than line 38 (estimate penalty amount) then the line 34 (overpayment amount) must equal the sum of lines 35a (refund amount), line 36 (amount applied to next year estimates), and line 38 (estimate penalty amount). If you have additional penalties and interest, please add them back into the amount on line 35a (refund amount) or line 36 (amount applied to next year estimates) in order to efile. (Rule Number: IND-073).
```

This happens when additional penalties and interest are being calculated.

## Solution

- In Organizer, select**Estimates and Penalties**, then**Penalties and Interest**.
- Go to the Additional Penalties and Interest section, remove the selection **Compute Interest on balance due** and **Compute interest on late filing penalty, if any**.
- In the Late Payment Penalty section, select **Do not compute the penalty**.
- In the Late Filing Penalty section, select**Do not compute the penalty**.
- In the Additional Penalties and Interest from Form 8978section, **Do Not Include Penalties and Interest from Form 8978**.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

  note

  This is an IRS limitation. They don't allow additional penalties and interest included in either the refund amount or the amount owed. The return will be rejected with additional penalties and interest included. This doesn't apply to the estimated tax penalty.

# E-file diagnostic: NOL Deduction statement

Learn how to complete the required Net Operating Loss (NOL) deduction statement when Schedule 1, line 8a contains an NOL deduction amount to resolve e-file errors.

```
Schedule 1: If there is a net operating loss deduction amount on line 8a, then the net operating loss carryforward deduction statement must have data in order to e-file. Navigate to Organizer \ Income \ Miscellaneous Income \ Miscellaneous Income \ Miscellaneous Income \ Button for NOL Statement (Rule Numbers: IND-368-01)
```

## Cause

This diagnostic occurs when Schedule 1, Line 8a has an amount but the data entry for the NOL deduction statement is missing.

## Solution

- Go to 

  **Tax forms****Federal****Sch 1**

   and confirm that **Line 8a** has an amount.

  note

  **Organizer****Income****Miscellaneous income**

  .
- Then go to **Miscellaneous income**, select **Miscellaneous income**.
- In the **Net Operating Loss** section, select **NOL Deduction Statement – Required**.
- Make the necessary data entries.
- Do a full recompute then recreate and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: SA-F1040-002

Learn how to attach Form 8283 when Schedule A, Line 12 noncash contributions exceed $500 to resolve e-file errors.

```
Schedule A: If Schedule A, Line 12 'Other than by Cash or Check' amount is greater than $500, then Form 8283 must be attached to Line 12. (Rule Number: SA-F1040-002)

This diagnostic occurs when there is an amount greater than $500 on Schedule A, line 12, and Form 8283 is not completed.

## Solution 1: Schedule A, line 12

  **Organizer****Itemized Deductions**

  .
- Go to 

  **Contributions****Contributions – CY and Carryovers**

  .
- Go to the **CURRENT-YEAR NONCASH CONTRIBUTIONS WHICH TOTAL LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO $500** section.

- Go to the **Section A Donated Property** or **Section B Donated Property** folder and add the information.
- Do a full recompute, then recreate the e-file.

## Solution 2: From a K-1

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Income**

  .
- Go to 

  **Schedule K-1****(name of K-1)****Schedule K-1 Information**

  .
- Go to the **Deductions** tab.
- Select **Noncash contributions $500 - $5000** or **Noncash contributions over $5000** and enter the information.
- Do a full recompute, then recreate the e-file.

articles.title: F1040-FW2G-009-01 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F1040-FW2G-009-01 e-file error

## Error

```
1040 federal Reject: FW2G-009-01: Form W-2G Line 14 has an amount, but there is not a state or state identification number entered.
```

## Cause

The Form W-2G has an amount entered on Line 14 (State winnings), but the corresponding state information is missing. This error occurs when there are state-specific winnings reported, but the system cannot associate these winnings with a particular state due to the missing information.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then select **Source Documents (W-2, 1099s, 1098)**.
- Select**W-2G**.
- For each W-2G form that has an amount on line 14:


  - Locate line 13
  - Enter the name of the state
  - Enter the state identification number
- Repeat step 4 for all relevant W-2G forms.
- Save the changes.
- Recompute the return.
- Attempt to e-file again.

articles.title: F1040-034-05 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F1040-034-05 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 1040, ‘WithholdingTaxAmt’ must be equal to the sum of the following: [(1) all ‘WithholdingAmt’ with corresponding ‘WithholdingCd’ having the value "FORM 1099" in the attached [OtherWithholdingStatment] and (2) all Forms W-2, ‘WithholdingAmt’ and (3) all Forms W-2G, ‘FederalIncomeTaxWithheldAmt’ and (4) Form 8959, ‘AddlMedcrRRTTaxWithholdingAmt’ and (5) ‘TotalAmt’ in [BackupWhSchedulesK1Statement] and (6) all Forms RRB 1042-S, ‘FederalIncomeTaxWithheldAmt’ and (7) all Forms SSA 1042-S (‘NetTaxWithheldAmt’ if it has a non-zero value, otherwise ‘FederalIncomeTaxWithheldAmt’)] unless Form 8958 is present in the return. When evaluating this, a tolerance of $5.00 is allowed. (value, rule F1040-34-05).
```

## Cause

This can be caused by an override on Form 1040 line 17, withholding on a form that can't be e-filed (such as Form 1042-S or 8288-A), or by an IRS error.

## Solution

- Select **Tax Forms**.
- Select **Federal**.
- Select **1040 — Income Tax Return**.
- Check line 17 for an override.


  - If it is overridden, remove the override, do a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# F1040-065-04 e-file error

```
Form 1040: To electronically file this return, you must have at least one of the following fields populated: Total Income, AGI, AGI Repeated, Tax, Total Credits, Total Tax, or Total Payments.
```

This happens when the IRS expects at least $1 on one of the lines in the e-file error message.

## Solution

- Make sure the fields listed in the e-file error message are correct.
- If you fix a mistake, recompute, recreate, and retransmit the return.
- If the lines are blank and correct, you need to paper-file the return.

# F1040NR-017 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 1040NR, WithholdingTxFrom8805Amt must be equal to the sum of all Forms 8805, TotalAllowedTaxCreditAmt (rule F1040NR-017)
```

## Cause

There's a difference between Form 1040NR and Form 8805 in this return, usually from forced data entry or a missing form.

## Solution

- Go to **Tax Forms**, then **Federal**.
- Select **1040NR - Nonresident Alien Income Tax**, then **Pages 1–5**.
- On **page 2**, line 62b (**Form 8805**), check if there's a manual data entry.
- If so, check it's correct and that Form 8805 is included with the return.
- Go to the **Organizer**, then select **Income**.
- Select**Schedule K-1**, then the entity.
- If the **Foreign Partners information** area is blank and the 8805 must be included, complete this information.
- Run a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

# F1040NR-027-01 e-file error

## Error

```
The sum of Form 1040NR, [ WagesSalariesAndTipsAmt and TotalOtherIncomeAmt and Schedule OI, TreatyTaxExemptUSIncomeAmt ] plus (+) the sum of Schedule NEC, [ DividendEquivalentPaymentAmt in IncomeTaxRt30UndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRtOthUndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRtOth2UndTrtyRuleGrp ] plus (+) [ OtherIncomeAmt in IncomeTaxRt10UndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRt15UndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRt30UndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRtOthUndTrtyRuleGrp and IncomeTaxRtOth2UndTrtyRuleGrp ] plus (+) the sum of all Schedule C (Form 1040), TotalGrossReceiptsAmt plus (+) Schedule C-EZ (Form 1040), TotalGrossReceiptsAmt must be greater than or equal to (the sum of all Forms 1042-S, GrossIncomeAmt with [(1) IncomeTypeCd having the value "17" or "18" or "19" or "20" or "23" or "25" or "26" or "27" or "32" or "35" or "38" or "40" or "41" or "42" or "43" or "44" and "54" and (2) ExemptionCd in Chapter3Grp not having the value "02" or "04"] plus (+) the sum of all Forms W-2, WagesAmt ). (rule 1040NR-027-01)
```

## Cause

This return meets these conditions:

* Has a Form 1040NR with a Form 1042-S that has income.
* Uses income codes 17, 18, 19, 20, 23, 25, 26, 27, 32, 35, 38, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, or 54.
* The income isn't reported on the 1040NR, Page 4, on the Dividend Equivalent line or on Schedule C.

## Solution

File the return on paper.

articles.body_md:
# F1040NR-SNEC-018 e-file error

## Error message

```
If there is no Form 1042-S with 'IncomeTypeCd' having the value "01" or "07" in the return and Form 1040NR, Schedule NEC, 'OtherInterestAmt' in 'IncomeTaxRtOthUndTrtyRuleGrp' or 'IncomeTaxRtOth2UndTrtyRuleGrp' has a non-zero value, then the corresponding 'TaxRt' must be greater than 30%.(value xx.xxxx rule F1040NR-SNEC-018)
```

note

The value represents the Schedule NEC rate below 30%.

## Cause

If there is not a Form 1042-S that has a 1 or 7 in Box 1, the rates on Schedule NEC lines 1 or 2, column d must be greater than 30%.

## Solution

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **Source Documents (W-2, 1099s, 1098)**.
- Select **1042-S**.
- Review Box 1, Income Code on each of the 1042-S forms.
- If incorrect, change the code. Then recompute the return, recreate the e-file, and submit the return.
- If the code is correct and isn't a 1 or 7, go to the **Organizer**, then **Foreign Information**, then **Nonresident Alien**.
- Select **Not Effect. Connected Inc - Other Rates**.
- Review the tax rate entered. It must be 30% or higher to e-file.
- If the tax rate is lower than 30% and there's not a Form 1042-S with code 1 or 7 in Box 1, the return can't be e-filed.

# F1116-004-02 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 1116 E-file: If Form 1116/1116AMT Line 10 has a non-zero value, then a PDF is required to be attached, with the description ‘Form 1116ScheduleB,’ and Section 951A income type must not be checked.
```

## Cause

Form 1116, line 10 has an amount greater than 0 so you must add an attachment.

Review Form 1116, line 10 for accuracy. If the amount is indeed greater than 0 and is correct, follow these steps to add an attachment to the return.

- Go to **Organizer**, **E-file**, **Attachments**, **PDF Attachments**, **Summary**, and select **Attach PDF**.

- Select Federal in the **Attachment Jurisdiction** dropdown.
- Select **Browse for file** and attach a Form 1116, Schedule B PDF.
- Select **Form1116ScheduleB** in the **Predefined description** dropdown.
- Select **Upload**, and then **Done**.
- Perform a full re-compute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.

# F4868-001-02 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 4868 can only be filed after the 'TaxPeriodEndDate' in the IRS Submission Manifest and on or before the due date to which the extension applies, unless Line 8 checkbox or Line 9 checkbox is checked.
```

## Cause

The extension can't be filed after the original due date unless line 8 or 9 is checked on Form 4868.

## Solution

If line 8 or 9 on Form 4868 applies and aren't checked, do the following:

- Go to **Organizer**, then **Payments and Extensions**.
- Open **Extensions**.
- For line 8, mark the **Taxpayer is out of the country and is a U.S. Citizen or resident** checkbox.
- For line 9, mark the **Taxpayer filed Form 1040NR and didn't receive wages subject to US income tax withholding** checkbox.
- Do a full recompute, recreate, and retransmit the return.

Form 8936, PrsnlUseNewCleanVehicleCrAmt must be equal to the sum of all Schedules A (Form 8936), PrsnlUseNewCleanVehicleCrAmt

* For Part IV, answer only question 6 and then the items under Part IV. Leave 5 and 7 blank.
* For Part V, answer Questions 6 and 7 and then items under Part V. Leave 5 blank.

articles.title: F8962-070 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F8962-070 e-file error

## Error

```
The e-file database indicates that Form 8962 or a binary attachment with description containing ‘ACA Explanation’ must be present in the return.
```

## Cause

The taxpayer received an Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) payment reported on Form 1095-A. Form 8962 reconciles APTC and, because it wasn't included in the return, the return is rejected.

note

The IRS has the ability to verify the receipt of the APTC payment before accepting the return. In the past, the return was accepted, and would later result in a notice sent to the taxpayer and recalculation of the refund or amount owed.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, select **Source Documents**, then **Form 1095-A**.
- Enter amounts for Form 1095-A.
- Next, attach a file with a description containing an **ACA Explanation**. Go to **Organizer**, **E-file**, **Attachments**, **PDF Attachments**, **Summary**, then **Attach PDF**.
- Select **Add**.
- Select **Federal** in the **Attachment Jurisdiction** dropdown.
- Select **Browse for file** and attach either Form 1095-A or Form 8962.
- Select **ACA Explanation** in the **Predefined description** dropdown, then select **Upload** and **Done**.
- Perform a full recompute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.

articles.title: IND-116-01 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# IND-116-01 e-file error

## Error

```
Each dependent in DependentDetail on the return with EligibleForChildTaxCreditInd checked needs to be under the age of 17. You may be eligible to claim the Credit for other dependents if you meet the requirements for the credit.
```

## Cause

If claiming the **Child Tax Credit** for any dependents, the dependent needs to be under the age of 17.

## Solution

If you want to claim the Child Tax Credit:

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
- Select **Dependents**, then **Dependent Input**.

  note

  If you used the Columnar Dependents Entry method, open that instead.
- Select the dependent causing the rejection.
- Check the **Social Security Number (or ITIN / ATIN)** field and make sure it is correct. If it isn't, correct it.

  note

  If the number in the field begins with any number between 900 and 999, it is an ITIN and therefore not eligible for the credit per [Publication 4164](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p4164.pdf).
- If the SSN is correct, paper file the return or contact the IRS e-Help Desk at 866-255-0654.

If you don't want to claim the Child Tax Credit:

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
- Select **Dependents**, then **Dependent Input**.

  note

  If you used the Columnar Dependents Entry method, open that instead.
- Select the dependent causing the rejection.
- Check that the **Qualifies for Child Tax Credit** and/or **Qualifies for Additional Dependent Needs** fields are empty.

articles.body_md:
# IND-144 e-file error

## Error

```
If 'ExcessSocSecAndTier1RRTATaxAmt' in the return has a non-zero value, then at least two Form W-2s with the same 'EmployeeSSN' must be present. (rule IND-144)
```

## Cause

There's an amount for excess Social Security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld, but there's only 1 W-2 included in the e-file for the employee.

## Solution

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **Source Documents** (W-2, 1099s, 1098).
- Select **W-2**.
- If there's only 1 W-2 for the employee with excess tax withheld, see IRS Topic No. 608, Excess Social Security and RRTA Tax Withheld.
- If there are 2 W-2s:


  - Make sure the Social Security number matches on both, and matches the taxpayer or spouse's SSN.
  - Check the Box 1 wages. If 1 of the 2 W-2s has 0 entered in Box 1, you'll need to paper file the return. The IRS doesn't allow W-2s with 0 wages to be included in the e-file.

- In the **Filing Status** section, remove the duplicate entry.
- Do a full recompute.
- Recreate the e-file.

# IND-452 e-file error

## Error

```
If AmendedReturnInd in the return is not checked, then the Primary SSN in the Return Header must not be the same as the TIN of a previously accepted electronic Individual return filed for the same tax period.
```

The IRS already has a return filed for this Social Security Number (SSN).

## Solution

# IND-516-01 e-file error

## Error

```
Incorrect Data: /Return/ReturnHeader/Filer/PrimarySSN: If Form 1040, 'PrimaryClaimAsDependentInd' is not checked, then the Primary SSN must not be the same as a Dependent SSN on another return. (value #########, rule IND-516-01)
```

note

The value indicates the SSN of the dependent causing the rejection.

## Cause

According to the IRS e-file database, the taxpayer's SSN has been used on a different return to claim a dependent exemption. For example, a student tries to file their own tax return and claim, after their parents filed a tax return and claimed the student as a dependent.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, **General Information**, then **Dependents**.
- Select **Dependent Input**.
- Find the dependent rejection value references.
- Check this dependent's **SSN**:


  - If the **SSN** is wrong, correct it, do a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.
  - If the taxpayer is not supposed to be claimed as a dependent, file the tax return on paper with Form 8948, and contact the IRS e-Help Desk at 866-366-0654 for more information.

## Error

```
An XML document that represents a binary attachment must have a valid reference to an attached file. (value, rule R0000-58-01).
```

note

The value will represent the PDF attachment causing the rejection.

## Cause

The file name of the PDF attachment doesn’t meet e-filing requirements.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **E-File**.
- Select **Attachments**, then **Summary**.
- Select **Attach PDF**.
- Check the files names of your PDF attachments meet the following e-file requirements:


  - 23 characters or less.
  - No spaces.
  - No special characters.
- If you need to change the file name of an attachment, delete it, make the change, then reattach it.
- Do a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

# R0000-142-01 e-file error

## Error

```
If you are a paid tax return preparer, you must use a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN) issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to identify yourself in the paid preparer section of the tax return. In future years, tax returns may be rejected if an SSN, or any number that is not a valid PTIN, is included in this field. (value, rule R0000-142-01),
```

## Cause

Paid tax return preparers must use a Preparer Tax Identification Number (PTIN) when they file a tax return.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **General Information**.

## Error

```
'PrimarySSN' and 'PrimaryNameControlTxt' in the Return Header must match the e-File database. (value #########, rule R0000-500-01)

note

The value represents the Social Security number of the person causing the rejection.

The IRS e-file database includes a name control and Social Security number for each filer. This rejection means that the information sent in the e-file doesn't match what the IRS has in the database.

- Select **Basic Return Information**, then **Taxpayer Information**.

  * Contact the IRS e-help desk at 866.255.0654 for more information.

articles.body_md:
# R0000-504-02 e-file error

## Error

```
Each 'DependentSSN' and the corresponding 'DependentNameControlTxt' that has a value in 'DependentDetail' in the return must match the SSN and Name Control in the e-File database. (value #########, rule R0000-504-02)
```

note

The value represents the Social Security number (SSN) of the dependent causing the rejection.

## Cause

The IRS e-file database includes a name control and SSN for each filer. This rejection means that the information sent in the e-file doesn't match what the IRS has in the database. This can happen if you enter the wrong name and/or SSN into GoSystem RS. Otherwise, there are a few possible causes that need to be worked out with the IRS or Social Security administration.

## Solution

If there's more than 1 dependent on the return, note the value at the end of the rejection. It will help you find the dependent causing the issue.

- In the **Organizer**, select **General information**, then **Basic Return Information**.
- Select **Dependents**, then **Dependent Input**.
- Find the dependent whose SSN was included in the rejection.
- Check to make sure that the **Last name** and **SSN** are correct.
- If the wrong information was entered, correct it. Then do a **Full Recompute** and e-file the return.
- If the information is correct:


  * If the dependent has multiple last names, refer to the Individual Name Control section of Publication 4164 for help on how to enter their last name.
  * Otherwise, advise the taxpayer (or legal representative) to contact the SSA at 800.772.1213 to verify the dependent's last name. If a correction is required, it may take the SSA up to 10 days to notify the IRS after they’ve updated their files. Afterward, an electronic return can be resubmitted.
- If you're unable to resolve the rejection, you can elect to bypass this error. You need the taxpayer's consent. If you do make this election, certain credits or exemptions may be disallowed, and return processing (including refund disbursement) may be delayed 4-6 weeks by the IRS. To make the election:


  - In the **Organizer**, select **E-file**.
  - Select **Additional Information**, then **Imperfect Return**.
  - Mark the **Imperfect return election** checkbox.

articles.body_md:
# R0000-507-01 e-file error

## Error

```
'DependentSSN' in 'DependentDetail' on the return was used as a Dependent SSN on a previously filed tax return for the same tax period. (value #########, rule R0000-507-01)
```

note

The value represents the Social Security number (SSN) of the dependent causing the rejection.

## Cause

The dependent SSN entered in the return was used on another return this year. This can happen because of incorrect data entry or because the dependent filed their own tax return.

## Solution

- Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
- Select **Dependents**, then **Dependent Input**.
- Verify that the dependent SSN information is correct. If it's correct and the dependent didn't file their own return claiming their exemption, contact the IRS e-Help Desk at 866.255.0654.
- Correct any wrong information. Then do a full recompute, re-create the e-file, and retransmit the return.

articles.title: Use the imperfect return election for ERC errors
breadcrumb: Use the imperfect return election for ERC errors
articles.body_md:
# Use the imperfect return election for ERC errors

Resubmit returns with ERC 0501 or 0504 validation errors by selecting the imperfect return election when dependent information doesn't match IRS records.

## When to use the imperfect return election

Use this election for returns that the IRS didn't process the 1st time due to ERC 0501 or 0504 validation errors. This election lets you resubmit even when dependent information doesn't match IRS records. These errors occur when:

* The child's Social Security number and family name on Schedule EIC don't match the IRS master file
* The dependent's Social Security number and family name on Form 1040/A don't match the IRS master file

On a subsequent filing with an ERC 0501 or 0504 error only, select the imperfect return election indicator and the IRS will process the return.

## What happens after you file

The IRS won't grant the credit or exemption in subsequent IRS reviews. Processing time is 4 to 6 weeks.

## How to make the election

To make the election, go to 

**Organizer****E-file****Additional Information****Imperfect Return**

.

# Error: The field “TaxpayerDaytimePhoneNum” with value '0', data is missing

This error occurs when the taxpayer's daytime phone number is invalid. The IRS requires a 10-digit phone number. The system sends "0" when no valid home phone number exists or the preferred contact option is set incorrectly.

## Error message

```
Validation failed on: Form: IRSPayment\[1]\[@documentId\='IRSPayment] TaxpayerDaytimePhoneNum\[1] Requirement: Taxpayer's Daytime Phone Number Requirement: Used for a phone no. - 10 digits Error: The field 'TaxpayerDaytimePhoneNum' with value '0', data is missing. # E-file diagnostic: Driver license/ID last four characters

Colorado Electronic Filing: Failure to include the driver license/ID last four characters, state of issue, and/or date of issue may delay the processing of the return.

  .
- Complete the **Driver's license or state issued ID number** field.

  Enter the last 4 characters, state of issue, and date of issue.
- Recompute the return to clear the diagnostic.

articles.body_md:
# CA extensions: General partner's phone number must be present e-file error

Resolve the California 1065 extension e-file error by entering the General Partner's phone number in Signature Information.

## Error message

```
CA Extensions: General Partner's phone number must be present. Navigation: Organizer>States>Common State>General Information>Basic Return Information>Signature Information tab
```

## Solution

California requires the General Partner's phone number to e-file the extension. Use the following steps to resolve this issue.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****States****Common State****General Information****Basic Return Information**

  .
- Select the **Signature Information** tab.
- In the row for California, enter a **Phone Number** in column G.
- Do a full recompute on the return.
- Recreate the extension e-file.

articles.title: F3801-020/020NR e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F3801-020/020NR e-file error

```
Rule Number F3801-020
California Form 3801: Federal rent/royalty/pass through income on Form 3801, page 2, line 2d does not equal federal rent/royalty/pass through income on Schedule CA, Section B, line 5, column A. If a full compute doesn't clear this diagnostic, review Form 3801 and Schedule CA.
```

```
Rule Number F3801-020NR
If Form 3801, Side 2, Line 2d amount is significant, then amount must equal Schedule CA (540NR), Part II, Section B, Line 5, column A.
```

This happens when the amount from Form 3801, page 2, line 2d doesn't match Schedule CA, section B, line 5, column A.

## Solution

To clear this diagnostic:

- Go to **Tax Forms** and select **States** then **California**.
- In the **Part-year Resident/Nonresident** folder, select **3801 - Passive Activity Loss Limitation**.
- Select **As if a resident**, then **Passive Activity Loss**.
- On the **Page 2** tab, and make note of the amount on page 2, line 2d.
- Next go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **California**, **Part-year Resident/Nonresident**, and then **Sch CA(540NR) - Adjustments**.
- Review the amount on Part II, Section B, line 5, column A. If it doesn't match Form 3801, enter an override.
- Perform a full re-compute, and re-create the e-file.

articles.title: 1280 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# 1280 e-file error

```
Idaho Form 43 Line 68: An income tax withheld from K-1 has been entered which indicates that a copy of Form(s) ID K-1 needs to be included with the tax return. This tax return cannot be e-filed. (Reject Code 1280)
```

This happens when there is withholding from a Schedule K-1 so the Form ID K-1 must be included but is not supported.

## Solution

- In Tax Forms, select **States**.
- Select **Part-year Resident/Nonresident**, then **43 – Income Tax Return**.
- Select **Page 3**, then line 68.
- If there is tax withheld on the Idaho return from a Schedule K-1, then Form ID K-1 must be attached. This form is not available in the system so you need to remove the amount or paper file the return.

  note

  PDF attachments of the ID K-1 will not clear the diagnostic.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

Illinois Schedule M and Schedules K-1-P and K-1-T: For all occurrences of the Schedule K1P and/or Schedule K1T, Schedule M Step 3 Line 14 "PartnerScorpEstateTrustLoss" must not be greater than the total amount of Schedule K1P Step 5 Line 38a Col A "InterestUSTreasuryBus" through Schedule K1P Step 5 Line 47 Col A "OtherSubtractions" and Schedule K1T Step 5 Line 36 Col A "InterestUSTreasuryBus" through Step 5 Line 45 Col A "OtherSubtractions." (Business Rule ILM-2000-1)

This happens when Schedule M, Page 2, line 14 amount doesn't equal the sum of partners of Schedule K-1-P or Schedule K-1-T.

  note

  If there's any overrides for these amounts, remove the overrides (such as NONE or even a spacebar override) on the tax forms.
- Perform a full re-compute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: Supported source documents are W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, etc.
breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Supported source documents are W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, etc.
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Supported source documents are W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, etc.

```
This return cannot be electronically filed and will be rejected. Return must be paper filed. E-file supported source documents are W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, W2-G and 1099-G.
```

This happens when the tax return includes withholding information from documents that are not supported for e-filing in Indiana, such as documents other than W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, W2-G, and 1099-G.

## Solution 1

To correct withholding sources for e-filing:

- In Tax Forms, select **States**, then **Indiana**.
- Select **Part-year Resident/Nonresident** , then **Sch F - Credits**, then drill down on line 1.
- Review the withholding sources and ensure that all of them are from W-2, 1099-R, 1099-Misc, W2-G, or 1099-G.
- Remove any withholding amounts reported from Schedule K-1s.
- Perform a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

## Solution 2

If you need to include withholding from Schedule K-1s you can't file the return electronically. You'll need to paper file the return to include the withholdings.
