articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: IA 8801 schema no longer nested inside the IA 148

```
Iowa IA 8801: As IA 8801 schema no longer nested inside the IA 148, when IA 8801 exist, tax credit code '09 Iowa Alternative Min Tax Credit' needs to be selected. and amount needs to be entered on IA 148 organizer. Go to Iowa Organizer / Credits / IA-148 Tax Credits.
```

This happens when credits are populated but no tax credit has been selected.

## Solution 1

If you don’t have tax credits to select,

- In **Tax Forms**, select **States**, then **Iowa**.
- Select **IA 8801 - PY AMT Credit**.
- The diagnostic is triggered when line 7 is populated with NONE. Override NONE by selecting the space bar so that line is blank. This clears the diagnostic without selecting a tax credit.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

## Solution 2

Check your IA 148 tax credits:

- In Organizer, select**States**, then **Iowa**.
- Select **Credits**, then **IA-148 Tax Credits**.
- In the **Schedule 148 Nonrefundable Credits** section, under **Credit name**, select tax credit code **09 Iowa Alternative Min Tax Credit (IA 8801)**.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.title: e-filing W-2, boxes 15 and 16
articles.body_md:
# e-filing W-2, boxes 15 and 16

```
Massachusetts W-2 entry: To e-file the state of Massachusetts, W-2 box 15 and Box 16, State and State Wages must be present. Please review the W-2 input. The State of Massachusetts verifies all income based off entries in the State Information Section of the W-2. Massachusetts assumes all income earned in any state will be associated with that state. If W-2 does not have any Massachusetts taxable wages go to Organizer/States/E-file/Additional Information and indicate W-2 does not contain state income.
```

This happens because Massachusetts requires W-2 wages to carry from boxes 15 and 16. If the W-2 doesn't have amounts in those boxes, the state advises to request a corrected W-2. All income should be reported in the state earned, not state taxable.

note

* NONE is not a valid entry.
* This can happen to other states, not just Massachusetts.

## Solution

To correct this error:

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **Massachusetts**, **E-File**, and then **Additional Information**.
- Select **W-2 contains no Massachusetts taxable income**.
- Perform a full re-compute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.

articles.title: 1047 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# 1047 e-file error

```
New York - Form IT-225: You have one of the following item for other additions or other subtractions. State did not assign specific code for these items. Code is always required for efile. You can't e-file this return. (Reject Code 1047) * Miscellaneous additions, Miscellaneous subtractions, Adjustment for income coded exempt for state purposes, Adjustment to income/loss from pass through entities (K-1 "State if different").
```

This happens when Form IT-225 – NYS Modifications Schedule A and B have an amount but the code is missing for an amount.

## Solution 1

Look for overrides or accidental entries in Schedule A:

- In Tax Forms , select **States**, then **New York**, then **Resident**.
- Select IT-225 – NYS Modifications, Page 1, Schedule A, Part 1, line 1, select the **Details** hyperlink.
- Clear any overrides and remove the amount on **Adjustments for income coded exempt for state purposes** since there is no code associated with this line.
- To edit this line, go to Organizer, select **States**, then **New York**, then **Part-year/Nonresident Allocation**.
- Select the **Part-year/Nonresident Allocation** tab, and then the Other Additions (New York Column).
- Perform a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

## Solution 2

Look for overrides or accidental entries in Schedule B:

- In Tax Forms, select 

  **States****New York**

  .
- Select Resident, IT-225 – NYS Modifications, Page 2, Schedule B, Part 1, line 10, then select the **Details**hyperlink.
- Clear overrides and amounts on **Adjustments for income coded exempt for state purposes**. Remove the amount since there is no code associated with this line.
- To edit this, go to Organizer, select **States**, then **New York**, then **Part-year/Nonresident Allocation**.
- Select the **Part-year/Nonresident Allocation** tab.
- Go to **Other Subtractions (New York Column**) and edit the amount.
- Perform a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

  note

  Per the state e-file schema, there are no assigned codes for the following items:


  * Miscellaneous additions
  * Adjustments for income coded exempt for state purposes
  * Miscellaneous subtractions
  * Adjustments to income/loss from pass-through entities (K-1 “State if different).

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: 149/4079
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: 149/4079

```
New York Electronic Return Signature: The E-File signature authorization for this return is incomplete. The ERO and Preparer must 'sign' this return by making a selection in the Persons Electronically Filing Main Return (Mandatory) area. GoSystem is professional software and ERO indicator is mandatory. Self-prepared by Taxpayer or Spouse option will not applicable. These fields are found by going to Organizers / States / New York / Electronic Filing / Additional Information tab. You can put "Self Prepared" for the name. (Reject code 149/4079)
```

This happens when the New York e-file is created, but the return signature section has not been filled out.

## Solution

- In Organizer, select **States**, then **New York**.
- Select **E-file**, then **Additional information**.
- If this is for an extension, in the section Signature Authorization, **Person(s) electronically filing extension (mandatory)**, select **ERO**. You need to have a selection and can't leave this as Not Applicable.
- For the option,**ERO Certification**, select **I have read the certification above and agree**.
- If this is for the return, go to the Return section, for the option **Person(s) electronically filing main return (Mandatory)** select an option other than Not Applicable.
- For the option**ERO / Preparer certification**, select **I have read the certification above and agree**.
- If the name of the ERO and Preparer are not the same, enter the name of the ERO.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

breadcrumb: Error: The attribute 'claimed' with value 'XXXXXX', data format is not correct
articles.body_md:
# Error: The attribute 'claimed' with value 'XXXXXX', data format is not correct

This New York e-file reject occurs when the paid preparer address contains special characters or exceeds the 29-character limit.

## **Error message**

```
Validation failed on AXXXXXX5.XNY:Form: rtnHeader: Requirement: Address Line format Error: The attribute 'claimed' with value 'XXXXXX', data format is not correct. Element Name: PREP\_LN\_1\_ADR XPath: /ReturnState\[1]/ReturnDataState\[1]/processBO\[1]/composition\[1]/forms\[1]/rtnHeader\[1]/PREP\_LN\_1\_ADR\[1] XML Fragment: Field Key: 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0 Error Code: 80004005 Error Reason: 'XXXXXX' violates pattern constraint of '\[A-Za-z0-9]\(\[A-Za-z0-9 \\-/]{0,29})'.The attribute 'claimed' with value 'XXXXXXX' failed to parse.[/STYLE]
```

## Solution

- Go to 

  **Organizer****General Information****Basic Return Information**

  .
- Select 

  **Paid Preparer Information****Firm Information****Address**

  .
- Remove special characters from the address field, including commas and periods.
- Shorten the paid preparer address to 29 characters or fewer.
- Do a full recompute to update the return calculations.
- Recreate the e-file.

note

Addresses with commas, periods, or more than 29 characters will cause the e-file to reject.

  If you don’t have a Webfile number or last year’s total revenue, you will need to contact the Texas Comptroller at (800) 442-3453.

articles.title: Correct validation errors with GoTo
articles.body_md:
# Correct validation errors with GoTo

Generate a validation file that uses GoTo functionality to go to the source of e-file errors and correct them efficiently.

When you create an e-file, the system identifies and reports validation errors. However, these error messages can be difficult to interpret, and locating where to make corrections may not be clear.

GoTo functionality solves this problem by letting you select a validation error and automatically go to its source—whether that's an Organizer field or a tax form. This saves time and eliminates guesswork when resolving e-file errors.

Follow these steps to create a validation file and resolve errors:

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Federal E-file****Error Checking**

  .
- Select **Generate Validation File**.
- For state returns, create the XML file with GoTo functionality separately in the 

  **State E-file****Validation**

   spreadsheet.
- After the system creates the validation file, go to 

  **View****Diagnostics****E-file Validation Errors**

  .
- Select a validation error to go directly to its source (Organizer or Tax Form field).
- If the error appears in a Tax Form field, select the link to the Organizer field and update it.
- Repeat these steps until you eliminate all validation errors.
- Select **Create E-file** to generate the final XML file for transmission.

  note

  * GoTo functionality is not available for XML files you create using **Create E-file**. To restore GoTo functionality, regenerate the validation file using the previous steps.
  * GoTo functionality doesn’t cover all XML validation errors. Product teams review and update this feature each filing season to include newly released errors.

articles.title: FPYMT-096 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# FPYMT-096 e-file error

```
If the timestamp (in the GTX key or Response to Send Submissions Request) is after the due date of the return (three and one half months after the Tax Period End Dt in the Return Header if the month in the Tax Period End Dt does not equal June), then the Requested Payment Dt in the "IRS Payment" [IRS Payment] must not be later than the date the return was received and must not be prior to five days before the date the return was received by the IRS
```

This happens when the Date to be debited entered is more than 5 days prior the submission or in the future date when the return was submitted.

## Solution

- In Organizer, select **General Information**, then **Bank Information** and return tab.
- In the **Direct Debit (Electronic Funds Withdrawal)** section, enter the date to be debited.
- Make sure the date need to be the day you submit the return or up to 5 days prior, but can't be in the future.
- Once done, full recompute and recreate the e-file

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: Federal K-1 E-file: There are less than 2 partners
breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Federal K-1 E-file: There are less than 2 partners
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Federal K-1 E-file: There are less than 2 partners

```
Federal K-1 E-file: There are less than 2 partners included in federal e-file. Based on the 2022 IRS schema, the IRS has removed the 2-partner minimum requirement if filing an Amended 1-65 return and filing Form 8082 with BBA AAR checked.
```

This happens when there aren’t at least two partners in the partnership, unless each of the following are true: (1) Form 1065, AmendedReturnID is checked and (2) Form 8082, DRAAARIND is checked.

**Solution**

As per the IRS E-File requirements, 1065s must have at least 2 partners to e-file. If at least 2 partners cannot be added, then the Federal Return will need to be paper filed. Please contact the IRS for more information.

- To enter partners, In Organizer, select **Partner Information**, then **Partner by Partner Data**.

  note

  Review Direct K-1 import by going to the folder.
- Select**Add new partner**.
- In Tax Forms, select 

  **Federal****Direct K-1 import****DK-1 Partner Review****DK-1 to Partner Information**

  .

  note

  Review or attach your K-1 aggregation file go to folder.
- In Organizer, select 

  **Federal E-file****Attachments****K-1 Aggregation****Attach K-1 Aggregation XML**

  .
- In the **Add** dropdown, select **Attach Jurisdiction**, then **Federal** and browse for the file. This opens another window.
- Find your file and select **Open**.
- In the Attachment Description area, select the predefined descriptions radio button and use the dropdown to select the filename. Select **upload**.

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: Partnership amounts for Income do not equal total of partners amounts
breadcrumb: E-file diagnostic: Partnership amounts for Income do not equal total of partners amounts
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Partnership amounts for Income do not equal total of partners amounts

```
Partnership amounts for Income do not equal total of partners' amounts: Please check the Reconciliation of Partnership to Partner Amounts.
```

This e-file error will show if the federal Partnership amounts for Income don’t equal total of partners' amounts or blank.

## Solution 1

Enable Partner Allocations:

- In Organizer, check if **Partner Allocations** are enabled. If not, select the checkbox for **Enable Partner Allocations**.
- Do a full recompute to apply the changes.

## Solution 2

Verify Override Amounts in Schedule K:

- Go to Organizer then **Sch K**.
- Make sure any overridden amounts match the amounts on Form 1065 Schedule K.
- Check Tax Forms for any overrides that affect the Schedule K.
- Do a full recompute to apply any changes.

## Solution 3

Review Income Summary for Allocation Codes:

- In Organizer go to **Sch K**, then **Income Summary** and open **Income summary**.
- If an allocation code for **Ordinary Income** has been entered read the associated warning for this item.
- Check for Over-Allocation in Income and Deduction Summary:


  - Go to Organizer then **Sch K**.
  - Select **Income Summary** then **Deduction Summary**
  - Make sure Allocation Codes haven’t been entered for total amounts and detail items that could cause overallocation.

    note

    * Don't allocate Other Interest income on the Income Summary tab.
    * Don't allocate detail lines for Other Interest Income on the Income Other Interest tab.
- Do a full recompute to apply any changes.

articles.body_md:
# E-file error: PartnerSSN

```
Form: IRS1065ScheduleK1[12][@documentId='IRS1065ScheduleK1N11] PartnerSSN[1]
Description: Partner's SSN
LineNumber: Schedule K-1 Part II Line E
Requirement: Type for Social Security No. - 9 digits
Error: The field 'PartnerSSN' with value 'XXXXXXXXX', data format is not correct.
```

You can get this error when the SSN or EIN isn't properly formatted.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer** and select **Partner Information**, then **Partner by Partner Data**.
- Select the partner's name that is causing the error. You can tell what partner it is from the error. Their SSN  or EIN is in the "Error: The field 'PartnerSSN' with value 'XXXXXXXXX', data format is not correct." portion of the error.
- Select **Partner Information**.
- In the 

  SSN \ EIN

   section, review what is selected in the 

  Options

   area.


  - If **SSN \ EIN (Default)** is selected, make sure the **SSN \ EIN (No other entry allowed)** field has a 9 digit number that isn't all 9s or 0s, and the hyphens are in the correct place.
  - If **Applied for** or **Foreign US Partner** is selected, then **SSN \ EIN (No other entry allowed)** should be empty.
- Do a full re-compute and re-create the e-file.

articles.title: Federal e-file status requested
articles.body_md:
# Federal e-file status requested

```
Federal e-file status requested.
```

You get this error during the IRS shutdown.

## Solution

Each year the IRS shuts down in December to prepare for the upcoming filing season and re-opens in January.

All returns submitted during the IRS shutdown will be received by Thomson Reuters and will have an electronic postmark at the time of receipt. These returns won't be submitted to the IRS and state agencies until the IRS re-opens in January.

note

This annual shutdown doesn't extend the IRS 10-day transmission perfection period.

articles.title: F7004-003-03 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F7004-003-03 e-file error

## Error

```
Form 7004, the application for extension can only be filed after the Tax Period End Date ("TaxPeriodEndDate" specified in the "ReturnHeader") and on or before the due date of the return to which the extension applies as specified in the Publication 4164. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule F7004-003-03)
```

## Cause

The extension was e-filed either before the tax year end or after the return due date. For example, on a return with a tax year end of 3/31, you'd receive this rejection if you filed an extension before 3/31 or after 6/15.

There will either be a mistake or override in the dates entered in the client, or the extension can't be filed now.

## Solution

Check for a mistake in the year-end date or an override in the extension date:

- Check the fiscal year-end date:


  - Go to the **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
  - Select **Basic Return Information**.
  - On the **Entity Information** tab, check the **Fiscal year ending date**. If the date is wrong, correct it. Otherwise, note it.
- Check the extension dates:


  - Go to the **Organizer**, then **Payments and Extensions**.
  - Select **Automatic Extensions**, then **7004 Basic Data**.
  - Make sure the override dates entered in the **Dates** section are correct. If any of the dates are wrong, correct them. Otherwise, note them.
- Compare the extension file date, the fiscal year-end date, and the extension date.


  - If the extension is too early to file based on the client's tax year end, wait until the appropriate date to file the extension.
  - If the extension is late or if the return due date has passed, file the return instead of the extension.

## Error

```
Form 7004, the tax year ending date (TaxPeriodEndDt specified in the Return Header) must match the data in the e-file database unless one of the checkboxes in Line 5b - "Initial Return", "Final Return" or "Consolidated return to be filed" is checked. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule F7004-904-01)

This error happens when the tax-period end date, the return type, or the EIN within the IRS database doesn't match the information in the electronic file. For example, the return may be a calendar year end 12/31/YY; however, the IRS's database shows the client's year end as a fiscal year end, 06/30/YY.

## Solution

Make sure the tax-period ending date, return type, and EIN are correct. If they are, contact the IRS e-Help Desk at 866.255.0654.

```

- Do a full re-compute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.

articles.title: R0000-035-01 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# R0000-035-01 e-file error

## Error

```
The 'TaxPeriodEndDt' in the Return Header must be less than the Received Date. (value YYYY-MM-DD, rule R0000-035-01).
```

## Cause

The tax year-end date within the rejected return is after the date on which the electronic file was received by the IRS. For example, a fiscal year return with a year-end date of April 30 must be received by the IRS after April 30.

## Solution

Follow these steps to check the year end:

- Go to **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
- Select **Basic Return Information**.
- Verify that the date in the **Fiscal year ending** field is correct.


  - If the date is wrong, correct it. Then do a **Full Recompute**, create the e-file, and submit the return.
  - If the date is right, call the IRS e-help Desk and 866.255.0654 and verify what they have on their record.

# R0000-058-01 e-file error

## Error

```
An XML document that represents a binary attachment must have a valid reference to an attached file. (value, rule R0000-58-01)

The file name of the PDF attachment doesn't meet e-filing requirements.

  * Remove and spaces in the name.
  * Remove any special characters.
- Delete and reattach any PDFs with name changes.
- Do a **Full Recompute**, create the e-file, and submit the return.

# R0000-068 e-file error

```
Federal 1065 MeF: If you use the PIN signature option (Form 8879-PE), you must enter the ERO's PIN, General Partner's PIN, Partner Name, Partner Title, Date Signed, and who entered the PIN number. R0000-068 Organizer General Information Basic Return Information Tab 'Signing General Partner or LLC Member Manager.'
```

This happens because signature information is missing or not carrying through to the return due to overrides.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, **General Information**, and then **Basic Return Information**.
- Select the **Return Information** tab.
- In the **Signing Partner or LLC Member** section, enter:


  - First name
  - Last name
  - Title
  - Date
- Next, go to **Federal E-file**, and **Signature Authorization**.
- In the **If Form 8879 - Practitioner PIN is selected** section, select either**General partner of LLC Member** or **ERO**.
- In the **PIN Information** section:


  - select **Randomly generate general partner or LLC PIN** and **Use first 5 numbers of firm EIN as ERO PIN**, or
  - manually enter both PINs.
- Perform a full re-compute and check if the diagnostic's been removed. If so, create the e-file and transmit. If the diagnostic still exists, continue to step 8.
- In **Tax Forms**, go to **Form 1065**.
- On the**Form 1065, Page 1** tab, check if there's any overrides in the signature area of the form. If overrides exist, remove them.
- Also review **Form 8879-PE** for any overrides and remove any that exist.
- Lastly, perform a full re-compute, create the e-file, and transmit the return.

articles.title: R0000-230 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# R0000-230 e-file error

```
IRS regulations require any entity with an EIN to update the Responsible Party Information within 60 days of any change by filing Form 8822-B, Change of Address or Responsible Party - Business. It is critical that the IRS have accurate Responsible Party Information in cases of identity theft or other fraud issues related to EINs or business accounts. For additional information on Responsible Parties visit the IRS website at: https://www.irs.gov/business/small-businesses-self-employed/responsible-parties-and-nominees.
```

This error can be either an informational e-file alert or an IRS rejection. Double-check that you have entered the correct EIN for this return.

## Solution

- If you get this error as an e-file alert:


  - Go to Organizer, then select Federal E-file.
  - Select **Additional Information**, then **Additional Information** again.
  - Select **Yes** for **Does the IRS have the most current Responsible Party information on file?**.
- If you get this as an error, it means the IRS database doesn't match the data in the electronic file. Check the information to make sure the following is correct:


  - tax period ending date
  - return type
  - EIN
  - business name control
- Re-compute and re-create the e-file.
- If the information you entered is correct, contact the IRS e-file help desk at (866) 255-0654 to verify what they have on file.

Filer's EIN and Name Control in the Return Header must match data in the e-File database, unless "Name Change" or "Name or Address Change" checkbox is checked, if applicable. (value #########, rule R0000-922-01)
```

## Cause

The IRS e-File database has a different EIN and Name Control combination on file.

## Solution

- Address or name change:


  - If the partnership changed its address or name, go to **Organizer**, then **General Information**.
  - Select **Basic Return Information**.
  - Mark the **Address change or Name change** checkbox.
- Check the name control:


  - Go to **Organizer**, then **Federal E-file**.
  - Select **Additional Information**, then **Business Name Control**.
  - If the **Business name control (Override)** field is completed, review Publication 4163 and make sure it's correct.
- Check the EIN:


  - Go to **General Information**, then **Basic Return Information**.
  - Make sure that the EIN field is correct.
- If you correct any field, do a **Full Recompute**. Then create the e-file and submit the return.
- If you aren't overriding the name control and the EIN is correct, call the IRS e-help Desk at 866.255.0654, and have them verify the client's EIN.

articles.title: Schedule K1- Partner Count e-file error
breadcrumb: Schedule K1- Partner Count e-file error
articles.body_md:
# Schedule K1- Partner Count e-file error

```
Rule Number: Schedule K1- Partner Count
Description: Number of Schedule K-1 value entered on Form PTE = X.
Actual Number of Schedule K-1 elements = X in the XML.
```

This diagnostic generates when the system detects that the number of Schedules K-1 included in the return does not match what is listed on that jurisdiction's main form. This can happen when K-1s are suppressed and there's no aggregation file attached.

## Solution

- In **Organizer**, select **General Information**.
- Select **Return and Print Options** and go to the **Sch K, K-1 and Activity Schedules** tab.
- In the **Print or Suppress** section, check if **Schedule K-1, partner activity schedules, and Schedule K-3** is marked as **Suppressed**.
- If they're suppressed, either change it to **Print**, or attach an aggregation file. To attach an aggregation file:


  - Select 

    **Federal E-file****Attachments****K-1 Aggregation****K-1 Aggregation**

    .
  - Select **Attach K-1 Aggregation XML File**.
- If they're not suppressed or you have an aggregation file attached, you can override the partner count. To do this:


  - Go to the **Basic Return Information** screen in the **General Information** folder.
  - Enter an amount in **Number of partners in partnership (Override)**.
- Do a full re-compute and e-file the return.

articles.body_md:
# SCHK2K3-013 e-file error

```
If [SchedulesK2K3Section743bBasisAdjustmentsStatement] is present in the return, then it must be referenced from one and only one of the following: Schedule K-2 (Form 1065) or Schedule K-3 (Form 1065) or Schedule K-2 (Form 8865) or Schedule K-3 (Form 8865).
```

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **Foreign Information**.
- Select **Ptr Distributive Share-International**, then **Other Tax Information-III**.
- Review each asset entered in **Sec 743(b) Basis Adj for Pos Inc Adj** and/or **Sec 743(b) Basis Adj for Neg Inc Adj**. Only assets from outside of the United States should be entered.
- For any assets where the source of income is from the United States:


  - Remove the amounts from here.
  - Go to **Other Tax Information**, also in the **Other Tax Information-III** folder.
  - Enter the amounts in the **U.S. source** fields for either section **A- Section 743(b) Positive Income Adjustment** or **B- Section 743(b) Negative Income Adjustment**
- This transfers to Schedule K-2, Page 8, Part III, Section 5.
- Perform a full recompute and recreate the Federal e-file.

articles.title: Severe Diagnostic: Beginning profit ratios do not foot
breadcrumb: Severe Diagnostic: Beginning profit ratios do not foot
articles.body_md:
# Severe Diagnostic: Beginning profit ratios do not foot

```
Beginning profit ratios do not foot to 1.0: Check beginning profit ratios entered in Organizer.
```

Make sure the beginning ratios add to 1.0. Zeros and NONE will also trigger this error.

## Solution

note

This is a severe diagnostic, it will not stop you from e-filing. Even if this is a first year filer beginning ratios are expected because the program is looking for the ratios at the beginning of the year.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Partner Information****Partner by Partner Data****Columnar Partner Entry**

  .
- Go to the **Ratios\Units** tab.
- Make sure the beginning ratios for the partners add up to 1.0.

# SK2-F1065-032 e-file error

```
If Schedule K-2 (Form 1065), 'OtherCategoryDescriptionCd' in 'SchK2K3InterestIncomeGrp', has a value of "XX", then the corresponding 'USSourceIncomeAmt' and 'ForeignBranchIncomeAmt' and 'PassiveCategoryIncomeAmt' and 'GeneralCategoryIncomeAmt' and 'OtherCategoryIncomeAmt' must be zero, if amounts are entered.

This happens when Schedules K-2 and K-3, Part II, Section 1 uses Code XX and an entry is made at other sources except for Sourced by partner line at Organizer, Foreign Information, then Ptr Distributive Share-International, Foreign Tax Credit Limitation-II, then Gross Income at By Country folder.

  note

  + If Aggregation file is being used, check the xml aggregation attachment for code XX, and may need to recreate the file, and reattach it to remove the rest of the K2 and K3 diagnostics.

articles.body_md:
# SK3-F1065-099 e-file error

You'll get this error if Schedule K-3 isn't correctly referenced in the return.

## Error message

```
Federal  
  Severity: Reject
  Form No: SK3-F1065
  Record Name: NA
  Form Occurrence No: 0
  Field Seq No: 0
  Page No: 1
  Reject Code: SK3-F1065-099
  Rule Number: SK3-F1065-099
  XML Path: //efile:IRS1065ScheduleK3[./@documentId = IRS1065ScheduleK3A1 ]
  Error Message: If Schedule K-3 (Form 1065) is present in the return, then it must be referenced from one and only one Schedule K-1 (Form 1065).
```

## Solution

- Go to 

  **Organizer****Partner Information****Common Partner Data**

  .
- In the **Defaults for All Partners** section, go to the **Attach Schedule K-3 to Schedule K-1 (Override)** subsection.
- Select an option other than **None Selected**.

- Verify each Schedule K-1 with a Schedule K-3 has Line 16 marked. If you're using Direct K-1, verify this under the **DK1** folder in **Tax Forms**.
- Verify there's a Schedule K-3 outputting in the XML for each Schedule K-1 that's marked.
- Verify that Schedule K-3 is aligned with each Schedule K-1, especially if you're using Direct K-1.

The taxing agency may send a notice requesting additional information from the taxpayer.

The XML data has failed schema validation.

This error can occur when the return doesn't conform to the IRS specifications for electronic filing.

Make sure there are no reject diagnostics or validation errors, then recompute and recreate the e-file. If you still get this error, contact Support.

This error can occur when the return doesn't conform to the IRS specifications for electronic filing.

Solution

Make sure there are no reject diagnostics or validation errors, then recompute and recreate the e-file. If you still get this error, contact Support.

articles.body_md:
# X0000-031 e-file error

## Error

```
Zip Entry names must conform to the guidelines in Publication 4164.
```

## Cause

A PDF attached to the return has an improper name or title.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **Federal E-File**.
- Select **Attachments**, **PDF Attachments**, then **Summary**.
- Select **Attach PDF**. Review your PDF attachments for the following e-file requirements:


  * Shorten the name of the attachments. File names should be 23 characters or less.
  * Remove any spaces in the name.
  * Remove any special characters.
- Delete and reattach PDFs with changed file names.

articles.title: 9967 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# 9967 e-file error

```
BinaryAttachment within the XML File (AttachmentLocation) Physical Attachments. Thomson Reuters Tax & Accounting has detected a discrepancy between the physical attachments and the attachment list within the e-File XML files.
```

This rejection typically generates when a PDF attachment doesn't meet name requirements. The file name of each PDF can't exceed 23 characters and can only contain letters and numbers.

## Solution

To fix this error, you'll need to take the following steps:

- Outside of the program, rename the file to shorten the name and remove any symbols or spaces.
- Within the locator, go to 

  **Organizer****States****[State]****E-file****PDF Attachments****Summary**

  .
- Select **Attach PDF**.
- Delete the attachment.
- Re-add the attachment.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the electronic file, and resubmit.

articles.title: State-903 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# State-903 e-file error

## Error

```
Electronic Filing Identification Number (EFIN) in the State Submission Manifest must be approved and present in the e-File database.
```

## Cause

The EFIN used in the return doesn’t match the IRS's e-file database.

## Solution

- Go to Organizer and select **States**.
- Select **State E-File** then **Enable/Create Returns**.
- Check that the EFIN entered is correct for each applicable state.
- If any EFIN is incorrect, fix it then recompute, recreate the e-file, and retransmit the return.
- If the EFIN is correct for each state, contact the IRS e-file help desk at (866) 255-0654.

# ALPPT-007a e-file error

```
AL E-File (PPT): ALPPT-007a: If Form PPT, Page 1, Line 5 is greater than or equal to 0 but less than or equal $100, you do not have a Business Privilege Tax filing requirement. Do not submit return, unless requesting a refund.
```

This happens because the business privilege tax is less than $100, which is under the filing threshold. You don't need to file Form PPT.

## Solution

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, **PPT**, **PPT, Page 1**, then **Line 5 (Privelege Tax Due)**.
- Review line 5 to make sure it is correct.
- If it is less than $100, and you don't need to file it, suppress the form.
- To suppress Form PPT is to do a space bar override on Line 5.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

This happens because the business privilege tax is less than $100, which is under the filing threshold. You don't need to file Form PPT.

Solution

  1. Go to
    Tax Forms
    ,
    States
    ,
    Alabama
    ,
    PPT
    ,
    PPT, Page 1
    , then
    Line 5 (Privelege Tax Due)
    .
  2. Review line 5 to make sure it is correct.
  3. If it is less than $100, and you don't need to file it, suppress the form.
  4. To suppress Form PPT is to do a space bar override on Line 5.
  5. Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

# E-file diagnostic: Partner's First Line Address, City, State/Country Code and ZIP Code must be present

```
AL E-File: According to AL Business Rules, Partner's First Line Address, City, State/Country Code and ZIP Code must be present. Please go to Organizer > Partner Information > Partner by Partner Data >Columnar Partner Entry to review the Partners' addresses.
```

This happens when you haven’t updated the partner address.

## Solution 1

- Select **Organizer**, **Partner Information**, then the**Partner by Partner Data** folder.
- Select **Columnar Partner Entry**.
- Then go to the **Name and Address** tab, in the **Partner Information** section.
- Enter the data in Columns **Partner Address**, **City**, **State**, and **ZIP Code** for all the partners.
- Do a full recompute.
- Recreate the e-file.

note

If you have foreign partners, leave **State** and **Zip Code** blank.

## Solution 2

- Select **Organizer**, **Partner Information**, then the **Partner by Partner Data** folder.
- Go to the **Partner Name** folder.
- Select **Partner Information**, then go to the **Partner Information** tab.
- Go to the **Name**, **Address**, **Phone Number and SSN \ EIN** section.
- Enter the **Partner Address**, **City**, **State** and **ZIP Code**.
- Do a full recompute.
- Recreate the e-file.

note

If you have foreign partners, leave **State** and **Zip Code** blank.

SK-AL65-028b: Form 65, Page 4, Schedule K Line 20c, if Alabama Amount (Apportioned Amount) is populated then the amount should equal to the detail total.

This happens when the sum of all shareholder's Part 3 Line Y amount isn't equal to the Alabama Apportioned Amount.

- Go to the **Tax Forms**, **States**, and the **Alabama** folder.
- Select **Form 65**, and go to the **65 Page 4**.
- Go to the **Schedule K** section.
- In the **20C Other Items and Amounts (attach Statement)** line, the amount must match the following line.
- Go to the **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, and the **Sch K-1** folder.
- Select **Partner Name**, and the sum of all shareholders **Part III Line Y** amount.
- Verify the values and make necessary changes in the following path.
- Go to the **Organizer**, **States**, and the **Alabama** folder.
- Select **State Adjustments**, and go to **Other** section enter the values.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

note

* Ensure that the form **65 Page 4**, **Sch K**, **Line 20C**, **Column C** amount must equal the total of the **Sch K-1**, **Part III**, **Line Y** amount.
* If you are using the **K-1 Aggregation** file, make the necessary changes in the **K-1 Aggregation** file and reattach it.

- Select **Organizer**, **States**, **Alabama**, then the **Electing Pass-Through Entity** folder.
- Select **General Information**, then mark the **Generate Electing Pass-Through Entity** checkbox.

- Select **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, then the **Sch K-1** folder.
- Select a **Partner Name**, then go to **Part III, Line Z Other items and amount**.

To change the value for **Line Z**, do the following:

- Select **Organizer**, **States**, then the **Alabama** folder.
- Select **State Adjustments**, then go to the **Income and Expenses** tab.
- Go to the **Other** section, then select **Other Items**.
- In the **Other Items Overrides** section, enter the **Amount** and **Allocation Code**.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

AL E-File: AL Reject Code SL-AL65-019: If AL 65, Page 5, Schedule L line 20b is populated, then a pdf document must be attached (File name and Predefined Name: OtherLongTermLiabilities.pdf) itemizing the separate categories and amounts of other current assets included in the total of current assets.
```

This happens when Alabama Form 65, Schedule L Line 20b is populated and the PDF attachment itemizing the separate categories and amounts of other liabilities included in the total of other liabilities is missing.

## Solution

- Select **Organizer**, **States** then **Alabama**.
- In the **Alabama** folder, go to **E-file - Form 65**, **Attachments**, **PDF Attachments**, **Summary**, then select **Attach PDF**.
- Add the PDF document named **OtherLongTermLiabilities.pdf**. The file name and description must be exactly the same.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# SPtecK1-ALPTEC-003a e-file error

```
SPtecK1-ALPTEC-003a: Form PTE-CK1, if the NRC-Exempt box is not populated, the Nonresident Entity Type is not Corporation "C", Exempt "E" or Individual Retirement Arrangement "IRA" and Column E, Total Income Amount is greater than zero, then Column F, Member's Tax Due MUST equal the product Column E, Total Income Amount multiplied by 5%; or if Column E, Total Income Amount is less than or equal to zero then Column F, Member's Tax Due must equal zero.
```

This happens when the Member's Tax Due is incorrect.

## Solution

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama** folder.
- Then **Composite Return** folder, go to **PTE-C Page 3**.
- Select **Partner Detail** hyperlink.
- Per on-screen instructions:


  * If a Nonresident owner/share holder has a loss, don’t include it.
  * Line H, Amount of Tax Due, must equal the product line F, Shareholder's Tax Due (Total Income X 5%, or if line F, Total Income Amount is less than or equal to zero then line H, Member's Tax Due must equal zero.
  * All partners should have an amount on line H. If partners don't have an amount on line H, they shouldn't be included in the composite.
- In Organizer, select **States**, then **Alabama**.
- Select **Composite return**, then**Composite return**.
- In the Return Options section, on line **Number of non-resident partners included in composite filing (Override)** , enter the data.
- In Organizer, select **Partner Information**, then **Partner by Partner Data**.
- Select the **Partner**, then **Partner Information**.
- In the State Composite Returns section, uncheck **Alabama**.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: ALPTEC-006: If Form PTEC Page 1 Line 1

```
ALPTEC-006: If Form PTEC Page 1 Line 1 (Amount of Tax Due) is populated (MUST have the same amount as Schedule PTE-CK1 Page 1 Line 15) then Line 4 (Total Tax) must equal the sum of Line 1 (Amount of Tax Due) plus Line 2 (Interest Due) and Line 3 (Penalty Due).
```

This happens when the amount on the PTE-C, page 1, line 1 does not match the amount on the PTE-C, page 3, line 15 .

## Solution

- Select **Tax Forms**, then the **States** folder.
- Select **Alabama**,then **Composite Return**, then the **PTE-C, Page 1** folder.
- Go to **line 1** and make note of the amount.
- Go to the **PTE-C, Page 3** folder.
- Go to **line 15** and check the amount. This amount needs to match the amount that's in **line 1** (found in step 3).
- If you need to make a correction to the total, select **Organizer** then the **States** folder.
- Select **Alabama** then the **Composite Return** folder.
- Select the **Composite Return** tab then go to the **Composite Options** section.
- Fill out the amount on the **Amount of tax due (override)** line.
- Run a full recompute, then recreate the E-file.

note

If you imported the K-1 on the return, make sure that all entries are correct from your imported file.

articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Federal return required

```
AL E-FILE: The State of Alabama requires federal return to be e-filed prior to e-filing AL Form 65. If the federal return is not e-filed then the AL return must be paper filed.
```

This happens when the Alabama e-file has been submitted before the federal return has been submitted.

## Solution

- Go to the **Returns** tab in the GoSystem browser.
- Select the return then select the **Info** tab.
- Select the **E-File Status** tab and make sure that the federal return shows as **Accepted**.
- If the Federal return isn't accepted, submit the Federal return and wait for it to be accepted.
- Select the **Returns** tab again and then open the return.
- Select **Organizer**, **States**, then **State E-File**.
- Select **Enable/Create Returns** and then select **Create** for Alabama.
- Recreate and resubmit the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# SK1-AL65-049 e-file error

```
SK1-AL65-049: AL Schedule K-1 Part III Line Z, the total number of K-1s marked NRC-Exempt should have the same number of Schedule NRCs generated in the XML file.
```

This happens when NCR exempt checkbox is marked but NRC forms are being included.

## Solution 1

If you’re doing a K-1 Aggregation:

- Select **Organizer**, then the **States** folder.
- Select **Alabama** then the **E-file-Form 65** folder.
- Select **Attachments**, **K-1 Aggregation**, then the **Summary** folder.
- Inside the Aggregation file, if the **NRCExempt** checkbox is marked, then NRC Forms need to be populated in the aggregation file.
- Once you've updated the aggregation file, remove the existing file and upload the fixed aggregation file.
- Run a full recompute, then recreate the E-file.

## Solution 2

If the K-1 is inside the return:

- Select **Organizer**,then the **Partner Information** folder.
- Select **Partner by Partner**, **Data**, select the partner name, then the **Partner Information** folder.
- Go to the **State Partner Information** tab.
- Go to the **Alabama** section and select **Include nonresident partner in Schedule NRC**.
- Run a full recompute, then recreate the E-file.

articles.title: E-file diagnostic: PTE-CK1- Partner Count
articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: PTE-CK1- Partner Count

```
Rule Number: PTE-CK1- Partner Count
Description: Form PTE-C, Number of non-resident partners value entered is = X,
Number of ScheduleK1 elements included in the XML file= X.
```

You can get this error when the number of partners on Form PTE-C don't match. You'll need to review data entry for the K-1.

## Solution 1

If nonresident partners don't have income, they shouldn't file the composite return. Per Alabama Instructions: If a Nonresident Owner/Shareholder has a LOSS, do not include him/her on Form PTE-C unless the loss is used to offset guaranteed payment(s)". It means only partners with positive income on Column (G) "Total Income" will be printing on this form. To make sure they have income check the following:

- In **Tax Forms**, select **States**.
- Select **Alabama**, then **Composite Return**.
- Select **PTE-C Page 3**, then open the **Partner Detail**.
- Under PTE-CK1, LINE E CALCULATION - SCHEDULE K-1 AMOUNTS, make sure the partner has a positive amount.

If there isn't an amount, remove the Composite return for that nonresident partner:

- Go to **Organizer** and select **Partner Information**, then **Partner by Partner Data**.
- Select the partner's name, then **Partner Information**.
- Select the **State Partner Information** tab and clear the checkbox for the Alabama composite return.
- In the **Partner by Partner Data** folder, select **Columnar Partner Entry**.
- Go to the **Partners State Composites** tab and remove any partners from the AL composite return that do not meet filing requirement.
- Make sure you don't have any overrides in 

  **Organizer****States****Alabama****Composite Return****Number of non-resident partners included in composite filing (Override)**

   field.
- Do a full re-compute and e-file the return.

## Solution 2

If filing the Alabama Composite:

- Go to 

  **Tax Forms****States****Alabama****Composite Return**

   folder.
- Select **PTE-CK1 Page 1**, then the **detail link** and make sure there is a value on Line G.
- Do a Full Recompute.
- Go to 

  **Organizer****Partner Information****Partner by Partner Data**

   folder.
- Select the folder for the partner, then **Partner Information**, then **State Partner Information**.
- Select the **Include nonresident partner in Schedule NRC** checkbox.
- Do a full Recompute.
- Recreate the E-file.

articles.title: SK1-AL65-008 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# SK1-AL65-008 e-file error

```
SK1-AL65-008: End Capital Account (EndCapitalAccount) should equal Beginning Capital Account (BegCapitalAccount) + Capital Contributed during the year (CapitalContributed) + Current year increase or decrease (CurrentYrIncrease) - Withdrawals and Distributions (WithdrawalsDistributions). (Automatic GOTO is not available). Please review your input Navigation: Tax Forms \ States \ Alabama \ Sch K1
```

This happens if the total input for Alabama is not equal to the formula mentioned in the error.

## Solution

- Select **Tax Forms**, **States**, then**Alabama**.
- Select **Sch K1** then **Partner name**.
- Go to **Part II** and locate **Line 8 Ending Capital Account**.
- Clear any **Overrides** for this line for all **K-1 Partners**.
- Make sure the **Ending Capital Account** equals the formula **[Beginning Capital Account + Capital Contributed during the year] + [Current-year increase or decrease - Withdrawals and Distributions]**.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

SK1-AL65-011: The total of all K-1s, Line G, Column 1, Ordinary Income (loss) should equal Schedule K, Line 1 Apportioned Amount.

- Select **Allocations**, **Special Allocations**, and **Add new special allocation code**.
- Enter the same allocation code as entered for the item you want to allocate. Then, enter an amount for each partner until 100% of the amount has been allocated.

note

If an aggregation file has been used to attach the form NC K-1 at **Organizer**, **States**, **Alabama**, **E-File**, **Attachments**, **K-1 Aggregation**, **Summary**. The aggregation file needs to be updated and reattached.

articles.title: SPtecK1-ALPTEC-005 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# SPtecK1-ALPTEC-005 e-file error

```
SPtecK1-ALPTEC-005: Form PTE-CK1 Page 1 Line 14 Col E must equal the sum of all Members' Share of Income Line E.
```

enter cause and intro (e.g. "This happens when" or "You get this error when")

## Solution 1

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, **Composite Return**, then **PTE-C, Page 3**.
- Select **Partner Details**. Remove the overrides on Line E.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit.

## Solution 2

- Per Alabama Instructions: **If a Nonresident Owner/Shareholder has a LOSS, do not include him/her on Form PTE-C unless the loss is used to offset guaranteed payment(s)**. It means only partners with positive income on Column (G) Total Income will print on this form.
- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, then **Sch K-1**.
- All partners need to have a positive amount or **NONE** entered on Part III Line G and Line M.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit.

## Solution 3

- Go to **Organizer**, **Partner Information**, **Partner by Partner Data**, **Columnar Partner Entry**, then the **Partner's State Composite** tab.
- Enter **X** for partners.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit.

## Solution 4

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, **Composite Return**, **PTE-C, Page 3**, then **PTE-CK1, Page 1**.
- Select **Partner Details**.
- All partners should have an amount on line G. If partners don't have an amount on line G, don't include them in the composite.

## Solution 5

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, **Sch K-1**, then **Partners**.
- If a partner doesn't have income from AL K-1, don't include them in the composite.

## Solution 6

- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Alabama**, **Composite Return**, **PTE-C, Page 3**, then **PTE-CK1, Page 1**.
- Select **Partner Details**.
- Negative amounts should not be included and each partner's Total income Amount needs to be 5% only.
- In Column H, **Member's Tax Due** needs to equal the product Column G, Total Income Amount multiplied by 5%. Or if Column G, Total Income Amount, is less than or equal to zero, then Column H, Member's Tax Due needs to equal zero.
- All partners should have an amount on line G. If partners don't have an amount on line G, don't include them in the composite. Non Composite or Non Resident partners should have no amounts on Line G.

## Solution 7

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **Alabama**, **Composite Return**, then the **Composite Return** tab.
- Go to the K-1 Aggregation or Import Use Only section.
- Populate the total from the Partner income (Column E) from the Attached File.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the e-file, and resubmit.

  If the ratios don't equal 100%, you'll need to file the return on paper.
- Select **View Schedule B Details**.
- Clear all overrides on the **Schedule B** yellow worksheet.
- Go to 

  **Organizer****Partner Information****Partner by Partner Data**

  .
- Select **Columnar Partner Entry**, then the **Ratios\Units** tab.
- Enter the **Federal partner Ownership%** to transfer to the **Alaska** return.

## Solution 2

Check for an aggregated Schedule K-1.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****States****Alaska**

  .
- Select **E-file, K-1 Aggregation**, then **Summary**.
- If the **System generated Schedule K-1s are disabled** and an aggregated XML file is present, select **Attach K-1 Aggregation XML File**.
- Select the aggregated XML file, then **RETRIEVE**.
- Update the aggregated XML file with the correct amounts so they’ll add up to the grand total.
- Delete the existing aggregated XML file from the electronic filing attachments screen.
- Select **Add**.
- Select **Attachment jurisdiction** for **Alaska K-1 Aggregation**.
- Select **Browse for file** and attach the updated XML Aggregation.
- Select **Upload**, then **Done**.

## Solution 3

Check for Direct K-1 Import.

- Go to **Organizer**, **Partner Information**.
- Select **Common Partner Data**.
- Select the **Direct K-1 Import** tab.

  note

  If the Direct K-1 Import tab isn't available, this option isn't available.
- If **Enable Direct K-1 Import to replace the computed Schedule K-1s** isn't turned on, then it's not being used.
- Update the import file and reimport the Direct K-1 Import file or go to 

  **Tax forms****States****Alaska**

  .
- Select **Schedule K-1** and change the amounts directly on the tax form.

# 2049 e-file error

If Form 1065 Page 1, line F, the "SALES FACTOR ONLY" box is checked, you must complete 1065 Page 3, Section C3 (Sales Factor) lines a through f.

- Once sales information is carried to Form 165, Page 3, Section C3, perform a full re-compute, and re-create the e-file.

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **Arizona**, **General Information**, and select the **Check if this Partnership is an Arizona-ONLY partnership** option.
- Do a full re-compute and re-create e-file.

articles.title: E-file error: Field ‘SchPartnrInfo’ is unexpected
articles.body_md:
# E-file error: Field ‘SchPartnrInfo’ is unexpected

```
Field 'SchPartnrInfo' is unexpected
```

## Cause

Form 1065: Prepare a schedule that lists each partner's name, address, taxpayer identification number and pro rata share of the amount.

Schedule D: the following fields are expected:

* Original Return Refund - OrigReturnRefund
* Total Payments - TotPaymnts
* Galance Of Tax Due - BalOfTaxDue
* Over Payment of PTI - OvrPaymentofPTE

## Solution

- Go to **Tax Forms**, then **States**, then **Arizona**, then **165**.
- Enter none for the following lines if they are blank.


  - 165 Page 2 line 25 (**Total PTE tax due by partnership**)
  - 165 Page 2 line 32 (**Balance of tax due, prior to penalties / estimates applied**)
  - 165 Page 3 line 37 **(total amount due, post penalties applied)**
- Do a full re-compute and re-create the e-file.

```
The field 'EndOfYr' with value 'NONE', data format is not correct.

- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# c00ce169 e-file error: Element name failed to parse

```
'XXXX' violates pattern constraint of '(([A-Za-z0-9#\-\(\)] & ') ?)*([A-Za-z0-9#\-\(\)] & ')'.
The element '{http://www.ftb.ca.gov/efile}Name' with value 'XXXX' failed to parse.
```

You may get this error a partner's name or address contains special characters.

## Solution 1

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **California**, **E-file**, **K-1 Aggregation**, then **Summary**.
- Remove any special characters from the partner names and addresses.
- Do a full recompute, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

## Solution 2

- Go to **Organizer**, **Partner Information**, **Partner by Partner Data**, **[Partner name]**, **Partner Information**, then the **Partner Information** tab.
- Go to the **Name, Address, Phone Number and SSN \ EIN** section.
- Remove any special characters from the partner's name.
- Do a full recompute, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# E-file diagnostic: Form 568 Schedule T: Tax due

```
Form 568 Schedule T: When using California 568 Schedule T aggregation, Form 568 Side 4 Schedule T Total tax due must have amount populated and must equal the sum of all Col G Net tax due from aggregation file
```

This happens when Form 568, Side 4, Schedule T, Total amount of tax due is incorrect.

## Solution

- Go to **Tax forms**, **States**, **California**, **568** and select **568**.
- Select the **568, Side 4** tab.
- In the **Schedule T** section, make a note of the total amount of tax due.
- Select the **Detail** link.
- Verify that the **Net Tax Due** column hasn't been overridden for any partners.
- The **total** for the **Net Tax Due** column should be equal to what is on **Schedule T, Total tax due**.

If a partner is showing in error, use the following steps.

- Go to **Organizer**, **Partner by Partner information**, **Name of partner**, and then **Partner information**.
- Select the **State information** tab.
- In the **California** section, deselect **Nonconsenting nonresident who did not sign Form 3832**.

articles.title: E-file error: California LLC Annual Tax: Form 8453-BE Part III cannot be NONE
breadcrumb: E-file error: California LLC Annual Tax: Form 8453-BE Part III cannot be NONE
articles.body_md:
# E-file error: California LLC Annual Tax: Form 8453-BE Part III cannot be NONE

```
e-File should only be generated and submitted when Form 8453-BE Part III Annual Tax payment have an amount and can't be NONE.
```

If you're filing the California LLC Annual return, Form 8453-BE needs to have payment information. There are 3 solutions.

## Solution 1

Make sure all bank information is correct.

- In **Organizer**, select 

  **States****Common State****General Information****Bank Information****Direct Debit**

   tab.
- Make sure **Authorization to Debit Funds** in column B is marked for the California PTE Tax.
- Make sure columns D-H are complete. Make sure the date in Column G, **Date Amount to be Debited** is the day of or after you submit the return.

## Solution 2

Make sure you're filing the correct form.

Use Form 8453-LLC to make annual tax, estimated fee, and/or PTE elective tax when e-filing Form 568 as one XML. Use Form 8453- BE (PMT) when making stand-alone payment, separate from Form 568.

* If you're using Form 8453-BE to file Estimated Fee Payment, create those separately in 

  **Organizer****States****State E-file****Enable/Create Estimates**

  .
* If you want to submit Annual Tax and estimated fee payment along with the main Form 568, then use Form 8453-LLC instead. Go to 

  **Organizer****States****California****Payment of Taxes****Form 8453-LLC Only**

   section.

## Solution 3

Suppress the California LLC Annual Tax return:

- Go to **Organizer** and select **States**.
- elect **State e-file**, then **Enable/Create returns**.
- Unmark **California Annual LLC** in column C.

articles.title: F565-060 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# F565-060 e-file error

## Error

You could get one of the following errors.

```
Form 565 [TaxPeriodBeginDate], [TaxPeriodEndDate], and [SOSNumber], or [FEIN] if [SOSNumber] is not present, from the CA-Return Header cannot match a previously accepted return unless Schedule Q [AmendedReturn] or [SupersededReturn] box is checked.
```

or

```
CA F565-060/F568-060: SOS ID or FTB Assigned ID number must be present. If no valid ID number, other reason (Foreign, Appl Applied for or Other reason) must be selected. Navigation: Organizer>States>California>General Information
```

## Cause

The state of California may already has a return on file for this filing period and Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN).

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then select **States**.
- Select **California**.
- elect **General Information**, then **General Information** again.
- In the **ID Options** section, make sure this section is filled out correctly.


  - Don't enter all 0's.
  - Don't use the FEIN as the SOS/FTB Assigned number.
  - If they don't have a valid ID#, leave the field empty and select **Other reason**.
- If the FEIN is incorrect, perform a full re-compute, re-create the e-file, then re-submit.
- If the FEIN is correct, contact the California Department of Revenue (DOR) at 800-852-5711.

CA Rule F565-067: Form 565, Side 1 Total asset at EOY must have data unless Side 2, Line P is checked "Yes".

- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

**Solution 2**

If your asset information is correct, and you don’t want to select **Yes**, then you need to paper file the return.

If Form 565 Question Q or Form 568 Question S is checked "Yes", then Schedule EO Part I must have data and ownership must be less than 100%.

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **California**, **Additional Information**, then **Questions**.
- Select **Yes** for Line BB/Z, **Does this partnership/LLC own an interest in a business entity disregarded for tax purposes?**
- Do a full recompute, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# F568-055 e-file error

## Scenario

You may get the following error message when submitting a return.

## Error

```
Form 568, filers Secretary of State Number [SOSNumber], LLC Temp Number [LLCTempNumber] or Not applicable reason [NotApplicable] in the CA-ReturnHeader must be present. (F568-055).
```

## Cause

California requires a valid Secretary of State number, LLC Temp number, or a **not applicable** reason to file the return.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer**, then **States**.
- Select **California**, then **General Information**.
- Select 1 of the following ID number options:


  * **Secretary of State ID number**.
  * **LLC temporary number assigned by FTB**.
  * An option from the **Select one of the following options if the entity does not have a state ID number** group.
- If you don't know the entity's Secretary of State ID number, contact the California E-Help Desk at 916-845-0353.
- Do a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

articles.body_md:
# SCHR-053 e-file error

## Scenario

You may get the following error message when submitting a return.

## Error

```
If Schedule R-1 Part A [StandardMethod] is present, then Line 2 column (c) [SalesApportionmentPercentage] must equal Line 1 column (b) [TotalSales] divided by Line 1 column (a) [TotalSales] multiplied by 100. Exception: If column (a) [TotalSales] and column (b) [TotalSales] are zero, then column (c) [SalesApportionmentPercentage] must be zero. (SCHR-053).
```

## Cause

There's most likely an override for an allocation and apportionment amount on Schedule R, Side 3, Part A. You can take the following steps to check this:

- Go to **Tax Forms**then select**States**.
- Select **California** then **565** or **568**.
- Select **Schedule R** then **Schedule R — Allocation and Apportionment**.
- Select **Sch R, Side 3 Part A**.

## Solution

- Go to **Organizer** then **States**.
- Select **California** then **Allocation and Apportionment**.
- Make either of the following changes:


  - Delete any overrides so the form calculates as intended.
  - Change line 1 in columns A and B so the computation equals the apportionment percentage override amount.
- Do a **Full Recompute**, re-create the e-file, and resubmit the return.

# X0000-010 e-file error

## Error

```
Your State submission does not match the latest published FTB Schema or is not well formed. You must contact your software provider to resolve this error.
```

## Cause

This return has missing or incorrect partner information entered for disregarded entities.

## Solutions

```
/CA-Return/CA-ReturnData/CAForm565ScheduleK-1/PartnerInformation/DisregardedEntity/NotApplicable
```

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **California**, and then **Partner Information**.
- Review partner information to ensure it's accurate. If a partner is designated as a disregarded entity, then you need to complete the **Disregarded Entity** section.

articles.title: Error: The field 'Loss' with value 'NONE', data format is not correct
breadcrumb: Error: The field 'Loss' with value 'NONE', data format is not correct
articles.body_md:
# Error: The field 'Loss' with value 'NONE', data format is not correct

This error occurs when the Loss field on California Form 565 or Form 568 Schedule EO contains an invalid value such as "NONE" instead of a valid decimal format. The California e-file schema requires loss percentages to be between 0% and 100%, entered as a decimal with up to 6 digits and 4 required fraction digits.

## Error message

```
Validation failed on [FILE_ID]:

Form: CAForm565ScheduleEO[1][@documentId='CAForm565ScheduleEO] PartialOwnership[1]/Loss[1]
Description: Loss Percentage
LineNumber: Part I
Requirement: CA type for a non-negative decimal that allows up to 6 digits and 4 required fraction digits
Error: The field 'Loss' with value 'NONE', data format is not correct.

Element Name: Loss
XPath: //CAForm565ScheduleEO[@documentId='CAForm565ScheduleEO']/PartialOwnership[1]/Loss[1]
XML Fragment: NONE
Field Key: 85,15661,132,0,0,0,0,0,0
Error Code: [CODE]
Error Reason: 'NONE' violates pattern constraint of '[0-9]?[0-9]?.[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'.
The element '{http://www.ftb.ca.gov/efile}Loss' with value 'NONE' failed to parse.
```

## Solution

- Go to 

  **Organizer****States****California****Other State Forms****Schedule EO****Part I - Partial Ownership of less than 100%**

  .
- Remove the NONE value from the **Loss** column. If there's no percentage or 0%, leave the field blank.
- Run a full recompute and create the e-file.

note

The percentages for partners can't be less than 0 or greater than 100% as per California's e-filing schema. Enter all ratios as fractions (for example, enter 23% as .23).

articles.body_md:
# Error: The attribute 'returnVersion' data format is not correct

This validation error occurs when the **returnVersion** attribute doesn't match the supported schema versions.

## Error message

```
Validation failed on [FILE_ID]:

Requirement: CA 568 Return - wraps around CA-Return Header 56X and CA-Return Data 568
Error: The attribute 'returnVersion' with value '2025v4.3', data format is not correct.

Element Name: CA-Return
XPath: /CA-Return[1]
XML Fragment: Field Key: 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0
Error Code: [CODE]
Error Reason: '2025v4.3' violates enumeration constraint of '2025v4.0 2025v4.1'.
The attribute 'returnVersion' with value '2025v4.3' failed to parse.
```

## Solution

Reset the California e-file setting to regenerate the return with a valid version.

- Go to 

  **Organizer****States****State E-file****Enable/Create Returns**

  .
- Unmark the **Enable** checkbox for California.
- Do a full recompute.
- Go back to 

  **Organizer****States****State E-file****Enable/Create Returns**

  .
- Remark the **Enable** checkbox for California.
- Do a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.title: 000054 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# 000054 e-file error

```
000054: FEIN cannot contain special characters or a value of nine of the same digit. Maximum detail items allowed for Taxes and License entries is limited to 20
```

As of 2023, IRS no longer allows FOREIGNUS to be e-filed.

## Solution

Navigate to the following sections and perform the specified actions:

In Organizer, go to:

- **Partner Information****Partner by Partner Data****Columnar Partner Entry****Name and Address****SSN/EIN**

  . Ensure each partner has a valid number entered. The number cannot consist of all 9s, 0s, or special characters. For EIN numbers, enter nine characters without any gaps or spaces.
- **Partner Information****Partner by Partner Data****Columnar Partner Entry****Partner****SSN/EIN**

  . Enter a valid number that cannot be all 9s, 0s, or "FOREIGNUS".
- If a partner does not have an EIN, select the drill down of that partner's EIN | SSN/EIN options and select **Applied for**.
- If the partner is a foreign partner and does not have a SSN or TIN, enter 000-00-0000 if the foreign partner is an individual, or 00-0000000 if the partner is an entity.
- After making these updates, perform a full recompute and recreate the FL E-file.

note

Even if the rejection is specific to Florida, it is necessary to fix the issue at the Organizer level for all partners' information to ensure compliance and accuracy in filing. After making these updates, perform a full recompute and recreate the FL e-file.

articles.title: Error: Field ‘Id’ is unexpected
articles.body_md:
# Error: Field ‘Id’ is unexpected

This e-file validation error happens when the Hawaii Tax ID number is missing or uses an incorrect format. The system expects a properly formatted Hawaii Tax ID (GE or W prefix).

## Error message

```
Validation failed on PXXXXXX5.XHI: Form: SchNP\[1] NPTable\[1]/Id\[1] Description: Id, Must be an SSN FormNumber: SchNP Table Requirement: Expecting IdType Error: Field 'Id' is unexpected Element Name: Id XPath: /ReturnState\[1]/ReturnDataState\[1]/SchNP\[1]/NPTable\[1]/Id\[1] XML Fragment: 123456789 Field Key: 110,676,129,0,0,0,0,0,0 Error Code: c00ce014 Error Reason: Element '{http://www.irs.gov/efile}Id' is unexpected according to content model of parent element '{http://www.irs.gov/efile}NPTable'. Expecting: {http://www.irs.gov/efile}IdType
```

## Solution

- Enter a valid Hawaii Tax ID number in

  **Organizer****States****Hawaii****General Information****Tax ID Number**

  .


  * If the ID starts with GE, use twelve digits.
  * If the ID starts with W, use eight digits.

  note

  If you don't have a valid Hawaii Tax ID number, contact the State of Hawaii for assistance. You'll need a valid ID before you can proceed with e-filing.
- Run a full recompute and re-create the e-file to clear related errors.
- Verify the Hawaii Tax ID on Form N-20 is formatted correctly:

  * GE + 12 digits
  * W + 8 digits

articles.title: HIXML-001 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# HIXML-001 e-file error

```
The XML data has failed schema validation. The file name of supporting binary attachments must match their name in the XML file.
```

This happens when Hawaii’s PDF Attachment names don't match its e-file schema requirements.

## Solution

Hawaii has a set of specific names for PDFs that it allows as attachments to its e-filed returns. If those names are not used, and only when required, then the return will get rejected.

- In **Organizer**, select **States**.
- Select **Hawaii**and then **E-file**.
- In **Attachments**, go to **PDF Summary** to review the attached PDF names.

Hawaii e-file attachment file names need to match the names listed in the instructions, starting on page 9 of 11.

Remove incorrect PDF attachments, rename the files outside the program, and then reattach to the state. Full recompute and recreate the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# IL1065-7200-2 e-file error

```
* IL1065-7200-2: Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 32 must equal all occurrences of Sch K1T Step 5 Lines 36a, 36b, 37, 38, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45 Column A, plus sum of all occurrences of Sch K1P Step 5 Lines 38a, 38b, 44, 45, 46, 47 Column A. Users must enter Sch K1P Step 5 or Sch K1T Step 5 in Organizer / States / Illinois / State Adjustments / Pass Through Input.
```

This happens when the amounts on Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 32 don’t match Sch K1T Step 5 Lines 36a, 36b, 37, 38, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45 Column A plus the sum of all Sch K1P Step 5 Lines 38a, 38b, 44, 45, 46, 47, Column A.

## Solution 1

- In **Tax Forms**, select the **States** folder.
- Select the 

  **Illinois****Sch K-1-P****(K-1 name)**

   folder.
- Go to the **Sch K-1-P, Page 2** tab.
- Take note of the amount on **Line 46 Column A**.
- Go to the **IL-1065** folder, then **IL-1065, Page 2** tab.
- Go to **Step 5**, **Line 32**.
- **Line 32** and **Line 46** mentioned earlier need to match for each K-1.

## Solution 2

- In **Organizer**, select the **States** folder.
- Go to the 

  **Illinois****State Adjustments****Pass Through Input**

   folder.
- Add a **K-1-P** or **K-1-T** and fill out the details.
- Go to **State Adjustments**, then **State Adjustment** folder.
- Remove any data under **Distributive share of additions** and **Distributive share of subtractions line**.
- Run a full recompute and recreate the e-file.

note

Grantor trusts should be included with individuals since they are disregarded and not taxed at trust rates.

articles.body_md:
# IL1065-8400-3 e-file error

```
IL1065-8400-3: If Form IL-1065 Step 6 Line 39 is greater than zero and Form IL-1065 Step 6 Line 40 and Form IL-1065 Step 6 Line 41 are zero, then Form IL-1065 Step 6 Line 42 must be 1.000000.
```

This happens when Form IL-1120 Page 2 Line 39 is greater than 0, and Lines 40 and 41 equal 0, then Line 42 needs to equal 1.000000.

## Solution

- Go to **Tax forms**, **States**, **Illinois** folder.
- Make sure that**Form IL-1065 Page 2 Step 6 line 42** doesn't say **NONE** unless **Line 39** is less than 0.
- If you need to enter **NONE** in this field, you need to file the return on paper.

As per the Form IL-1065 Instructions, for Line 42: Divide **Line 41** by **Line 40** and enter the result, rounded to 6 decimal points. The result can't be greater than 1 or less than 0.

Refer to the [Illinois 1065 Instructions](https://tax.illinois.gov/content/dam/soi/en/web/tax/forms/incometax/documents/currentyear/business/partnership/il-1065-instr.pdf) for more information.

```
FormIL1065 Step 9 Line 65c must equal the sum of all occurrences of SchILK1T Step 7 Line 49 plus sum of all occurrences of SchILK1P Step 7 Line 55.
```

This happens when Form IL-1065, Step 9, Line 61b (pass-through withholding payments reported to you on Schedule(s) K-1-P or K-1-T) isn't included in the e-file or the detail doesn't tie to the total.

## Solution

Go to 

**Organizer****States****Illinois****State Adjustments**

 to enter detail for Schedule K-1-P and/or K-1-T:

- Select the **Pass Through Input** folder.
- Add a new Schedule K-1-P and/or Schedule K-1-T under the appropriate folder.


  - For **Schedule K-1-P**, enter the amount under the section for Step 7 - Share of Illinois credits and recapture and pass-through entity payments in the field for 54 Pass-through withholding payment.
  - For **Schedule K-1-T**, enter the amount under the section for Step 7 - Share of pass-through entity payments in the field for 49 Pass-through entity payment.
- In the **State Adjustments** folder, go to the **Net Income and Tax** screen.
- Go to the **Penalties and Payments** section.
- Review any entry in the **Pass-through entity payment (override)** field. Any entry in this field needs to match the total for any Schedules K-1-P and/or K-1-T.
- Perform a full re-compute, re-create the e-file.

articles.body_md:
# IL1065-4600-1e-file error

```
If Form IL-1065 Step 3 Line 11 (Total) is greater than zero, then you may have reported an IRC Section 965(c) deduction listed on Line 3 of the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement. Please email the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement to rev.BitSupplemental@illinois.gov. If you fail to provide the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement, the item of expense reported on Form IL-1065 Step 3 Line 11 (Total) will be disallowed and a Return Correction Notice will be issued requesting the statement for verification. The IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement is required to reinstate the item of expense.
```

This happens if the amount on Form IL-1065 Step 3 Line 11 is greater than 0. You may need to provide a supplemental statement via email to the state.

## Solution

If you reported an IRC Section 965(c) deduction on Line 3 of the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement, email the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement to [rev.BitSupplemental@illinois.gov](mailto:rev.BitSupplemental@illinois.gov).

If you fail to provide the IRC 965 Transition Tax Statement, the expense item reported on Line 11 (Total) of Step 3 on Form IL-1065 will be disallowed, and a Return Correction Notice will be issued requesting the statement for verification.

note

This error won’t prevent you from e-filing. If it doesn’t apply to the return, you can disregard it.

# IL1065-5700-2 and IL1065-7200-2 e-file errors

```
reject code IL1065-5700-2,If Form IL-1065 Step 4 Line 19 is greater than zero, then Form IL-1065 Step 4 Line 19 must equal all occurrences of Sch K1T Step 5 Lines 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 Column A, plus sum of all occurrences of Sch K1P Step 5 Lines 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 Column A. reject code IL1065-7200-2,If Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 32 is greater than zero, then Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 32 must equal all occurrences of Sch K1T Step 5 Lines 36a, 36b, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46 Column A plus sum of all occurrences of Sch K1P Step 5 Lines 38a, 38b, 44, 45, 46, ,47 Column A.
```

These diagnostics generate when Form IL-1065, Step 4, Line 19 and/or Step 5, Line 32 have data, but Schedule K-1-P or Schedule K-1-T information has not been added to the return.

## Solution

- In **Organizer** go to **States** then **Illinois**.
- Select **State Adjustments** then **Pass Through Input**.
- If you haven't already added a **Schedule K-1-P** or **Schedule K-1-T** and the information to support Form IL-1065, Step 4, Line 19 and/or Step 5, Line 32, do so now.

# IL1065-6400-1 e-file error

```
IL1065-6400-1: If Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 27 is greater than zero, then Sch B Section A Line 3 must be greater than zero.
```

This happens when the value of Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 27 is not equal to Sch B Section A Line 3.

## Solution 1

- Go to the **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Illinois** folder.
- Select **IL-1065**, then go to **IL-1065, Page 2**.
- Go to **Step 5, In Line 27** if you have a value greater than 0.
- **Step 5, Line 27** value must equal the following line.
- Go to **Tax Forms**, **States**, **Illinois** folder.
- Select **Schedule B**, then go to **Schedule B, Page 1**.
- Go to **Totals from Schedule B**, **Section B**, and review the amount in **Line 3**.

note

If **IL-1065, Page 2, Step 5 Line 27** is greater than 0, then **Form IL-1065 Step 5 Line 27** must equal **Sch B Section B Line 3**.

## Solution 2

Check for an aggregated Schedule K-1.

- Go to **Organizer**, **States**, **Illinois**.
- Go to **E-file**, **K-1 Aggregation**, and select **Summary**.
- If the system-generated Schedule K-1s aren't available and an aggregated XML file is present, select **Attach K-1 Aggregation XML File**.
- Select the aggregated XML file, then **Retrieve**.
- Update the aggregated XML file to have the correct amounts so they’ll add up to the grand total.
- Delete the existing aggregated XML file from the electronic filing attachments screen.
- Select **Add**.
- Select **Attachment Jurisdiction for NOS K-1 Aggregation**.
- Select **Browse for file** and attach the updated **XML Aggregation**.
- Select **Upload**, then **Done**.

## Solution 3

Check for Direct K-1 Import.

- Go to **Organizer**, **Partner Information**.
- Select **Common Partner Data**.
- Look for a tab called **Direct K-1 Import**.


  - If you don’t see the **Direct K-1 import** tab, it's not enabled.
  - If you do see the **Direct K-1 import** tab, select it.
- If the option to **Enable Direct K-1 Import to replace the computed Schedule K-1s** is not available, it's not being used.
- If it is available, update the import file and reimport the Direct K-1 Import file or go to 

  **Tax forms****States****Illinois**

  .
- Select **Schedule K-1** and change the amounts directly on the tax form.

articles.title: IL1120B-2700-4 e-file error
articles.body_md:
# IL1120B-2700-4 e-file error

You'll get this error if on Schedule B, Page 2, any partner that has a code A, C, M, N, P, or S under Column B has an SSN entered under Column C.

## Error message

```
If the partner or shareholder is a disregarded entity for federal income tax purposes (ex: grantor trust, single member LLC, etc), then the owner of the disregarded entity s information and designation should be entered as the partner or shareholder for purposes of the schedule B. Example, if the partner or shareholder is a grantor trust and is owned by an individual, then the partner or shareholder should be designated as an I for individual. This will help to insure the proper amount of pass-through withholding will be calculated for nonresident partners and shareholders. (IL1120-2700B-4)
```

## Solution

note

This reject code is only an alert and will not cause the e-file to be rejected.

- Go to 

  **Tax Forms****States****Illinois****Sch B-Partner Identification****Schedule B****Page 2****Sch B detail link**

  .
- Any partner that has a code A, C, M, N, P, or S in Column B can't have an SSN entered in Column C. Make sure Column C is blank for that partner.
- If a partner is designated as a **Trust** but an SSN has been entered rather than an EIN, you can do 1 of the following:


  * Enter an FEIN.
  * Change the entity type to **Grantor Trust**, which Illinois treats as individuals.
- Do a full recompute, recreate the electronic file, then resubmit the return.
